1.176.d:
संश्रावितस्तेन तथैव वाक्यं स रावणो नाम विरोधकाले ॥
उल्लंघ्य वाक्यं निधनं जगाम धर्मे स्थितस्या प्रतिमप्रभावः ॥21॥
1.199
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
प्रहेतितनयो राजन्पुलोमा नाम विश्रुतः ॥
क्रोधदृष्ट्या तु यः शीघ्रं च्यवनेन विनाशितः ॥1॥
वज्र उवाच ॥
च्यवनेन किमर्थं वै पुलोमा राक्षसो हतः ॥
कथं च भृगुशार्दूल तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 2 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
पुलोम्नो दानवेन्द्रस्य द्वे कन्ये भुवि विश्रुते॥
पुलोमा भृगवे दत्ता शची दत्ता च वासवे ॥3 ॥
कन्याभावे रुदन्तीं तु कदाचिद्यदुनन्दन ॥
पुलोमामुक्तवान्राजन्पुलोमा दानवेश्वरः ॥ 4 ॥
हे रक्षः कन्यकामेतां गृह्णीष्व रुदतीं बलात् ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु पुलोम्नो भवनाजिरे ॥ 5 ॥
छिद्रान्वेषी दुराचारः पुलोमा स व्यतिष्ठत ॥
अनुसृत्य च जग्राह तां कन्यां चारुलोचनाम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.176.m:
Likewise was that Rāvaṇa made to hear words by him at the time of hostility; / disregarding his words, though established in dharma and of incomparable power, he met with destruction.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The son of Praheti, O king, was renowned by the name Puloman, / who was quickly destroyed by Cyavana with a wrathful glance.
Vajra said: / For what reason was the rākṣasa Puloman killed by Cyavana, / and how, O tiger among the Bhṛgus? Explain that to me as I ask.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Two daughters of Puloman, the lord of the dānavas, were renowned on earth: / Pulomā was given to Bhṛgu, and Śacī was given to Vāsava.
Once, when she was crying in her maidenhood, O delight of the Yadus, / Puloman, the lord of the dānavas, said to Pulomā, O king:
"Hey rakṣas, seize by force this maiden who is crying!" / At that very time, in the courtyard of Puloman's palace,
that wicked Puloman stood, looking for an opportunity; / and having approached, he seized that lovely-eyed maiden.

1.176.s:
nirbhartsya taṃ durācāraṃ pulomā dānavottamaḥ ..
kālena pradadau kanyāṃ bhṛgave tāṃ sumadhyamām .. .7 ..
antarvatnīṃ tu rahitāṃ bhṛguṇā tāmaninditām ..
agnihotragatāṃ dṛṣṭvā pulomāgnimathābravīt .. 8 ..
paulomī yadi matpūrvā seyaṃ pāvaka śaṃsa me ..
tāmagnirabravīttasya seyaṃ patnī bhṛgoḥ śubhā .. 9 ..
evamagnerbhṛgoḥ śrutvā tāṃ jahāra sa rākṣasaḥ ..
tasyāṃ tu dṛśyamānāyāṃ garbhaḥ kukṣestadā cyutaḥ .. 1.199.10 ..
cyavanāccyavano nāma babhūva sa mahātapāḥ ..
dṛṣṭamātrastu tenā'sau pulomā bhasmasādgataḥ .. 11 ..
pulomāśrunipātena nadī jātā vadhūvarā ..
vahniśca sarvabhakṣyatvaṃ bhṛguśāpādupāgataḥ .. 12 ..
hutāśanastu saṃkuddhaśśāpaṃ prāpya dvijottamāt ..
lokakāryaratirbrahmā svayaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 13 ..
1.176.d:
निर्भर्त्स्य तं दुराचारं पुलोमा दानवोत्तमः ॥
कालेन प्रददौ कन्यां भृगवे तां सुमध्यमाम् ॥ .7 ॥
अन्तर्वत्नीं तु रहितां भृगुणा तामनिन्दिताम् ॥
अग्निहोत्रगतां दृष्ट्वा पुलोमाग्निमथाब्रवीत् ॥ 8 ॥
पौलोमी यदि मत्पूर्वा सेयं पावक शंस मे ॥
तामग्निरब्रवीत्तस्य सेयं पत्नी भृगोः शुभा ॥ 9 ॥
एवमग्नेर्भृगोः श्रुत्वा तां जहार स राक्षसः ॥
तस्यां तु दृश्यमानायां गर्भः कुक्षेस्तदा च्युतः ॥ 1.199.10 ॥
च्यवनाच्च्यवनो नाम बभूव स महातपाः ॥
दृष्टमात्रस्तु तेनाऽसौ पुलोमा भस्मसाद्गतः ॥ 11 ॥
पुलोमाश्रुनिपातेन नदी जाता वधूवरा ॥
वह्निश्च सर्वभक्ष्यत्वं भृगुशापादुपागतः ॥ 12 ॥
हुताशनस्तु संकुद्धश्शापं प्राप्य द्विजोत्तमात् ॥
लोककार्यरतिर्ब्रह्मा स्वयं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 13 ॥
1.176.m:
Having rebuked that wicked one, Puloman, the best of the dānavas, / in time gave that slender-waisted maiden to Bhṛgu.
Seeing that blameless woman pregnant and alone, separated from Bhṛgu, / when she had gone to the agnihotra, Puloman then spoke to Agni:
"If she is Paulomī, previously mine, declare this to me, O Fire!" / Agni said to him, "She is the auspicious wife of Bhṛgu."
Having thus heard from Agni of Bhṛgu, that rākṣasa carried her off. / While she was being taken, the foetus fell from her womb then;
from falling (cyavana) he became named Cyavana, of great ascetic power. / No sooner was he seen by him than that Puloman was reduced to ashes.
From the falling of Pulomā's tears, the river Vadhūsaras was born, / and fire came to be the devourer of all through the curse of Bhṛgu.
Then the fire, having received the curse from that foremost of the twice-born, became enraged; / Brahmā, devoted to the welfare of the worlds, himself spoke these words:

1.176.s:
vahne tavārcibhiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ śuci sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati ..
śucibhūtaṃ tataḥ paścādbhakṣayiṣyatyasaṃśayam .. 14 ..
etattavoktaṃ cyavanasya janma nāśastathā rākṣasapuṅgavasya ..
vahneḥ śucitvaṃ ca tathārciṣāṃ vai vaṃśaṃ pulomno'tha nibodha rājan .. 15 ..
1.200
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
pulomnastanayaḥ śrīmānmadhurnāma niśācaraḥ ..
viniṣkṛṣya svakācchūlācchūlaṃ prādādvṛṣadhvajaḥ .. 1 ..
tapasā toṣito yasya saputrasya mahātmanaḥ ..
trailokyavijayāsakte tena rājendra rāvaṇe ..2 ..
dīkṣite meghanāde ca tathā yāte nikumbhilām ..
antarjalagate vīre tathaiva ca vibhīṣaṇe .. 3 ..
nidrāvaśagate rājankumbhakarṇe suradviṣi ..
mālinastanayā tena rāvaṇasya svasā hṛtā .. 4 ..
kumbhīlasī mahābhāgā rūpadraviṇasaṃyutā ..
yasyāmasya suto jajñe lavaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ .. 5 ..
1.176.d:
वह्ने तवार्चिभिः स्पृष्टं शुचि सर्वं भविष्यति ॥
शुचिभूतं ततः पश्चाद्भक्षयिष्यत्यसंशयम् ॥ 14 ॥
एतत्तवोक्तं च्यवनस्य जन्म नाशस्तथा राक्षसपुङ्गवस्य ॥
वह्नेः शुचित्वं च तथार्चिषां वै वंशं पुलोम्नोऽथ निबोध राजन् ॥ 15 ॥
1.200
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
पुलोम्नस्तनयः श्रीमान्मधुर्नाम निशाचरः ॥
विनिष्कृष्य स्वकाच्छूलाच्छूलं प्रादाद्वृषध्वजः ॥ 1 ॥
तपसा तोषितो यस्य सपुत्रस्य महात्मनः ॥
त्रैलोक्यविजयासक्ते तेन राजेन्द्र रावणे ॥2 ॥
दीक्षिते मेघनादे च तथा याते निकुम्भिलाम् ॥
अन्तर्जलगते वीरे तथैव च विभीषणे ॥ 3 ॥
निद्रावशगते राजन्कुम्भकर्णे सुरद्विषि ॥
मालिनस्तनया तेन रावणस्य स्वसा हृता ॥ 4 ॥
कुम्भीलसी महाभागा रूपद्रविणसंयुता ॥
यस्यामस्य सुतो जज्ञे लवणो नाम राक्षसः ॥ 5 ॥
1.176.m:
"O Fire, everything touched by your flames shall become pure; / having thus become pure, it will thereafter undoubtedly be consumed."
Thus the birth of Cyavana has been told to you, as well as the destruction of that foremost rākṣasa, / and the purity of fire and of its flames; now learn, O king, the lineage of Puloman.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Puloman had an illustrious son, a night-roamer named Madhu; / the bull-bannered [Śiva], pulling a trident from his own trident, gave it to him,
pleased by the asceticism of that great-souled one along with his son. / When Rāvaṇa was bent upon the conquest of the three worlds, O best of kings,
and Meghanāda was consecrated [for ritual] and had gone to Nikumbhilā, / and the heroic Vibhīṣaṇa was immersed within the waters,
and Kumbhakarṇa, the enemy of the gods, had fallen under the power of sleep, O king, / Rāvaṇa's sister, the daughter of Mālinī, was carried off by him—
the highly fortunate Kumbhīnasī, endowed with beauty and wealth; / in her, a son was born to him, a rākṣasa named Lavaṇa,

1.176.s:
yena śūlaprabhāveṇa māndhātā vinipātitaḥ ..
na tasya putro bhāryā vā babhūvātidurātmanaḥ .. 6 ..
prāṇināṃ puruṣādyānāṃ sahasrairdaśabhirnṛpa ..
āhāramāhnikaṃ tasya bhavatyaudarikasya tu .. 7 ..
rāmājñayā tasya babhūva rājanrāmānujo mṛtyuradīnasattvaḥ..
śatrughnanāmā bhuvanasya vīro mahāntarastho hariraprameyaḥ .. 8 ..
1.176.d:
येन शूलप्रभावेण मान्धाता विनिपातितः ॥
न तस्य पुत्रो भार्या वा बभूवातिदुरात्मनः ॥ 6 ॥
प्राणिनां पुरुषाद्यानां सहस्रैर्दशभिर्नृप ॥
आहारमाह्निकं तस्य भवत्यौदरिकस्य तु ॥ 7 ॥
रामाज्ञया तस्य बभूव राजन्रामानुजो मृत्युरदीनसत्त्वः॥
शत्रुघ्ननामा भुवनस्य वीरो महान्तरस्थो हरिरप्रमेयः ॥ 8 ॥
1.176.m:
by whom, through the power of that trident, Māndhātṛ was struck down. / That exceedingly evil-souled one had neither son nor wife.
With ten thousand living beings, beginning with humans, O king, / the daily meal of that glutton was made.
By Rāma's command, the younger brother of Rāma, endowed with noble courage, became his death, O king— / the hero named Śatrughna, who was the immeasurable Hari residing within another form.

1.177.s:
1.201
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
yakṣe rākṣase jāte tataḥ kālena kenacit ..
eṣā suṣāva gandharvaṃ śailūṣamiti viśrutam ..1 ..
1.177.d:
1.201
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
यक्षे राक्षसे जाते ततः कालेन केनचित् ॥
एषा सुषाव गन्धर्वं शैलूषमिति विश्रुतम् ॥1 ॥
1.177.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / After the yakṣa and the rākṣasa were born, then in the course of time / she gave birth to a gandharva well known as Śailūṣa.

1.177.s:
koṭyastisrastu putrāṇāṃ tasyāsansudurātmanaḥ ..
etasminneva kāle tu visṛṣṭāsu prajāsu ca .. 2 ..
1.177.d:
कोट्यस्तिस्रस्तु पुत्राणां तस्यासन्सुदुरात्मनः ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु विसृष्टासु प्रजासु च ॥ 2 ॥
1.177.m: Three tens of millions of sons were born to that exceedingly evil-souled one. / At that very time, when the creatures had been created,

1.177.s:
brahmādideśa rājyāni jātyāṃ jātyāṃ yathākramam ..
gandharvāṇāmadhipatiṃ cakre citrarathaṃ tathā .. 3 ..
1.177.d:
ब्रह्मादिदेश राज्यानि जात्यां जात्यां यथाक्रमम् ॥
गन्धर्वाणामधिपतिं चक्रे चित्ररथं तथा ॥ 3 ॥
1.177.m: Brahmā assigned kingdoms to each class in due order; / and so he made Citraratha the overlord of the gandharvas.

1.177.s:
śailūṣaputrā gandharvā saṃghaśaḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ ..
śāsanenaiva tiṣṭhanti tasya citrarathasya tu .. 4 ..
1.177.d:
शैलूषपुत्रा गन्धर्वा संघशः कृतनिश्चयाः ॥
शासनेनैव तिष्ठन्ति तस्य चित्ररथस्य तु ॥ 4 ॥
1.177.m: The gandharvas, the sons of Śailūṣa, resolved in multitudes, / remained [defiant] toward the command of that Citraratha.

1.177.s:
sindhorubhayakūleṣu deśamutsādya te tadā ..
hatvā ca manujāṃstatra nivasanti gatavyathāḥ .. 9 ..
1.177.d:
सिन्धोरुभयकूलेषु देशमुत्साद्य ते तदा ॥
हत्वा च मनुजांस्तत्र निवसन्ति गतव्यथाः ॥ 9 ॥
1.177.m: Devastating the country on both banks of the Sindhu, / and having killed the men there, they lived without distress.

1.177.s:
utsādayanto rāṣṭrāṇi rājñāṃ vipriyakārakāḥ ..
tāñśaśāpa sa gandharvarājaścitrarathaḥ prabhuḥ .. 6 ..
1.177.d:
उत्सादयन्तो राष्ट्राणि राज्ञां विप्रियकारकाः ॥
ताञ्शशाप स गन्धर्वराजश्चित्ररथः प्रभुः ॥ 6 ॥
1.177.m: Because they were devastating realms and causing displeasures to kings, / the powerful Citraratha, king of the gandharvas, cursed them:

1.177.s: adharmaniratāḥ sarve mānuṣādvadhamāpsyatha ..7..
1.177.d: अधर्मनिरताः सर्वे मानुषाद्वधमाप्स्यथ ॥7॥
1.177.m: "You who are devoted to unrighteousness shall all meet your death at the hands of a human."

1.177.s:
śāpena tasyāpratimena rājangandharvarājāti balasya saṃkhye ..
babhūva mṛtyurbharatastu teṣāṃ dehāntarastho hariraprameyaḥ .. 8 ..
1.202
vajra uvāca ..
śailūṣaputrā gandharvā bharatena kathaṃ hatāḥ..
kimarthaṃ tu mahābhāga tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ ..1..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ayodhyāyāmayodhyāyāṃ rāme daśarathātmaje ..
kaikeyādhipatiḥ śrīmānyudhājinnāma pārthivaḥ .. 2..
rāmāya preṣayāmāsa dūtaṃ bharata mātulaḥ ..
vṛddhaṃ purohitaṃ gārgyaṃ yena kāryeṇa tacchṛṇu ..3..
sindhorubhayakūleṣu rāmadeśo manoharaḥ ..
hatvā raṇe manuṣyendrāngandharvairviniveśita..4..
gandharvāste ca rājendra rājñāṃ vipriyakārakāḥ ..
lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ vāpi śatrughnamathavā nṛpa .. 5 ..
visarjayitvā gandharvāṃstānvināśaya rāghava ..
rājāno nirbhayāḥ santu deśaścāstu tathā tava .. 6 ..
1.177.d:
शापेन तस्याप्रतिमेन राजन्गन्धर्वराजाति बलस्य संख्ये ॥
बभूव मृत्युर्भरतस्तु तेषां देहान्तरस्थो हरिरप्रमेयः ॥ 8 ॥
1.202
वज्र उवाच ॥
शैलूषपुत्रा गन्धर्वा भरतेन कथं हताः॥
किमर्थं तु महाभाग तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥1॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अयोध्यायामयोध्यायां रामे दशरथात्मजे ॥
कैकेयाधिपतिः श्रीमान्युधाजिन्नाम पार्थिवः ॥ 2॥
रामाय प्रेषयामास दूतं भरत मातुलः ॥
वृद्धं पुरोहितं गार्ग्यं येन कार्येण तच्छृणु ॥3॥
सिन्धोरुभयकूलेषु रामदेशो मनोहरः ॥
हत्वा रणे मनुष्येन्द्रान्गन्धर्वैर्विनिवेशित॥4॥
गन्धर्वास्ते च राजेन्द्र राज्ञां विप्रियकारकाः ॥
लक्ष्मणं भरतं वापि शत्रुघ्नमथवा नृप ॥ 5 ॥
विसर्जयित्वा गन्धर्वांस्तान्विनाशय राघव ॥
राजानो निर्भयाः सन्तु देशश्चास्तु तथा तव ॥ 6 ॥
1.177.m:
By the matchless curse of that extremely mighty king of the gandharvas, O king, / Bharata, who was the immeasurable Hari residing in another body, became their death in battle.
Vajra said: / How were the gandharvas, the sons of Śailūṣa, slain by Bharata? / And for what reason, O highly fortunate one? Explain that to me as I ask.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / While Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, was in unconquerable Ayodhyā, / the glorious ruler of the Kaikeyas, a king named Yudhājit,
Bharata's maternal uncle, sent an envoy to Rāma— / his aged family priest, the descendant of Garga; hear for what purpose:
"On both banks of the Sindhu, O Rāma, is a charming land; / having killed the lords of men in battle, it has been settled by gandharvas.
And those gandharvas, O best of kings, are doing displeasures to kings. / Either Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, or Śatrughna, O king,
having dispatched, destroy those gandharvas, O descendant of Raghu, / so that kings may be free from fear, and that land may become yours."

1.177.s:
dūtasya vacanaṃ śrutvā cintayāmāsa rāghavaḥ ..
meghanādavadhe karma lakṣmaṇena mahatkṛtam .. 7 ..
śatrughnena kṛtaṃ karma lavaṇaṃ ca vinighnatā..
preṣayiṣyāmi bharataṃ gandharvasya ca nigrahe ..8..
1.177.d:
दूतस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा चिन्तयामास राघवः ॥
मेघनादवधे कर्म लक्ष्मणेन महत्कृतम् ॥ 7 ॥
शत्रुघ्नेन कृतं कर्म लवणं च विनिघ्नता॥
प्रेषयिष्यामि भरतं गन्धर्वस्य च निग्रहे ॥8॥
1.177.m:
Hearing the envoy's speech, the descendant of Raghu reflected: / "A great deed was performed by Lakṣmaṇa in the slaying of Meghanāda;
a deed was performed by Śatrughna when he struck down Lavaṇa; / I shall send Bharata to subdue the gandharvas."

1.177.s:
ityevaṃ manasi dhyātvā rāmo bharatamabravīt ..
gaccha gārgyaṃ puraskṛtya vatsa rājagṛhaṃ svayam ..9..
1.177.d:
इत्येवं मनसि ध्यात्वा रामो भरतमब्रवीत् ॥
गच्छ गार्ग्यं पुरस्कृत्य वत्स राजगृहं स्वयम् ॥9॥
1.177.m: Reflecting thus in his mind, Rāma said to Bharata: / "Placing the descendant of Garga in front, child, go yourself to Rājagṛha.

1.177.s:
mātulena samāyuktaḥ kaikayendragṛhāttataḥ ..
jahi śailūṣatanayāngandharvānpāpaniścayān .. 1.202.10 ..
1.177.d:
मातुलेन समायुक्तः कैकयेन्द्रगृहात्ततः ॥
जहि शैलूषतनयान्गन्धर्वान्पापनिश्चयान् ॥ 1.202.10 ॥
1.177.m: Joined with your maternal uncle, setting forth from the abode of the Kaikeya lord, / slay the sons of Śailūṣa, the gandharvas of evil resolve."

1.177.s:
evamuktaḥ sa dharmātmā bharato bhrātṛvatsalaḥ ..
rāmasya pādau śirasā cābhivandya kṛtāñjaliḥ .. 11 ..
1.177.d:
एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः ॥
रामस्य पादौ शिरसा चाभिवन्द्य कृताञ्जलिः ॥ 11 ॥
1.177.m: Addressed thus, the righteous Bharata, fond of his brother, / bowed to Rāma's feet with his head and with folded hands;

1.177.s:
gṛhaṃ gatvā cakārātha sarvaṃ prāsthānikaṃ vidhim ..
oṣadhīnāṃ kaṣāyeṇa tadotplāvitavigrahaḥ .. 12 ..
1.177.d:
गृहं गत्वा चकाराथ सर्वं प्रास्थानिकं विधिम् ॥
ओषधीनां कषायेण तदोत्प्लावितविग्रहः ॥ 12 ॥
1.177.m: going home, he then performed the entire departure rite. / His body was then bathed with a decoction of herbs;

1.177.s:
gaurasarṣapakalkena prasāditaśiroruhaḥ ..
tīrthasārasanādeyaiḥ salilaiśca sa sāgaraiḥ .. 13 ..
1.177.d:
गौरसर्षपकल्केन प्रसादितशिरोरुहः ॥
तीर्थसारसनादेयैः सलिलैश्च स सागरैः ॥ 13 ॥
1.177.m: his hair was cleansed with white mustard paste; / and with waters from holy bathing-places, rivers, and oceans,

1.177.s:
candanasrāvasammiśraiḥ kuṃkumākṣodasaṃyutaiḥ ..
sarvauṣadhisamāyuktaiḥ sarvagandhasamanvitaiḥ .. 14 ..
1.177.d:
चन्दनस्रावसम्मिश्रैः कुंकुमाक्षोदसंयुतैः ॥
सर्वौषधिसमायुक्तैः सर्वगन्धसमन्वितैः ॥ 14 ॥
1.177.m: mixed with liquid sandalwood, blended with saffron powder, / combined with all medicinal herbs, endowed with all perfumes,

1.177.s:
mantrapūtairmahātejāḥ sasnau rāghavavardhanaḥ ..
śaṅkhabherī ninādena paṇavānāṃ svanena ca .. 15 ..
1.177.d:
मन्त्रपूतैर्महातेजाः सस्नौ राघववर्धनः ॥
शङ्खभेरी निनादेन पणवानां स्वनेन च ॥ 15 ॥
1.177.m: and purified by mantras, he of great splendor, the enhancer of the Raghus, bathed / to the sounding of conches and kettledrums, to the noise of paṇava drums,

1.177.s:
ānakānāṃ ca śabdena nisvanena ca bandinām ..
sūtamāgadhaśabdena jayakāraistathaiva ca .. 16 ..
1.177.d:
आनकानां च शब्देन निस्वनेन च बन्दिनाम् ॥
सूतमागधशब्देन जयकारैस्तथैव च ॥ 16 ॥
1.177.m: to the sound of ānakas, and to the ringing cries of bards, / to the sound of sūtas and māgadhas, and with shouts of victory.

1.177.s:
tuṣṭavuḥ snānakāle taṃ stavairmaṅgalapāṭhakāḥ ..
tathopatasthurgītena gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 17 ..
1.177.d:
तुष्टवुः स्नानकाले तं स्तवैर्मङ्गलपाठकाः ॥
तथोपतस्थुर्गीतेन गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 17 ॥
1.177.m: At the time of the bath, reciters of benedictions praised him with hymns, / and troops of gandharvas and apsarases attended him with song.

1.177.s:
snātaḥ sa bharato lakṣmyā yuvarājābhirūpayā ..
vilipya cārusarvāṅgaṃ candanena sugandhinā .. 18 ..
1.177.d:
स्नातः स भरतो लक्ष्म्या युवराजाभिरूपया ॥
विलिप्य चारुसर्वाङ्गं चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ॥ 18 ॥
1.177.m: Having bathed, that Bharata, endowed with the splendor suited to a crown prince, / anointed his handsome limbs all over with fragrant sandalwood;

1.177.s:
ahatāmbarasaṃvītaḥ śvetamālyavibhūṣaṇaḥ ..
kuṇḍalī sāṅgadī maulī sarvaratnavibhūṣitaḥ .. 19 ..
1.177.d:
अहताम्बरसंवीतः श्वेतमाल्यविभूषणः ॥
कुण्डली साङ्गदी मौली सर्वरत्नविभूषितः ॥ 19 ॥
1.177.m: clothed in unwashed garments, adorned with white garlands, / wearing earrings, armlets, and a diadem, adorned with all jewels,

1.177.s:
antasthaṃ pūjayāmāsa devadevaṃ trivikramam ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpādikarmaṇā..1.202.20..
1.177.d:
अन्तस्थं पूजयामास देवदेवं त्रिविक्रमम् ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपादिकर्मणा॥1.202.20॥
1.177.m: he worshipped the God of gods, Trivikrama, residing within, / through the rites of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lights, and the rest.

1.177.s:
pūjayitvā jagannāthamupatasthe hutāśanam ..
suhutaṃ brāhmaṇendreṇa rāghavāṇāṃ purodhasā .. 21 ..
1.177.d:
पूजयित्वा जगन्नाथमुपतस्थे हुताशनम् ॥
सुहुतं ब्राह्मणेन्द्रेण राघवाणां पुरोधसा ॥ 21 ॥
1.177.m:
Having worshipped the Lord of the World, he approached the fire,
which had been well-offered by the foremost brahmin, the family priest of the Raghus.

1.177.s:
gobhirvastrairhiraṇyaiśca turaṅgakaripuṅgavaiḥ ..
modakaiḥ saphalairdadhnā gandhairmālyaistathākṣataiḥ .. 22 ..
1.177.d:
गोभिर्वस्त्रैर्हिरण्यैश्च तुरङ्गकरिपुङ्गवैः ॥
मोदकैः सफलैर्दध्ना गन्धैर्माल्यैस्तथाक्षतैः ॥ 22 ॥
1.177.m:
With cows, garments, gold, excellent horses and elephants,
with modakas accompanied by fruit, curds, perfumes, garlands, and unbroken grains,

1.177.s:
svastivādyāṃstathā viprānmahātmā bhūridakṣiṇaḥ ..
vyāghracarmottare ramye sūpaviṣṭo varāsane .. 23 ..
1.177.d:
स्वस्तिवाद्यांस्तथा विप्रान्महात्मा भूरिदक्षिणः ॥
व्याघ्रचर्मोत्तरे रम्ये सूपविष्टो वरासने ॥ 23 ॥
1.177.m:
the great-souled one, bountiful in sacrificial fees, [honoured] the brahmins chanting benedictions;
then, seated well on an excellent seat covered with tiger-skin,

1.177.s:
āyudhānantaraṃ cakre dhvajacchatrābhipūjanam ..
svastikānvardhamānāṃśca nandyāvartāstathaiva ca .. 24 ..
1.177.d:
आयुधानन्तरं चक्रे ध्वजच्छत्राभिपूजनम् ॥
स्वस्तिकान्वर्धमानांश्च नन्द्यावर्तास्तथैव च ॥ 24 ॥
1.177.m:
after the weapons, he worshipped banners and parasols,
as well as svastikas, vardhamānas, and nandyāvarta emblems,

1.177.s:
nadyaḥ kāñcanavinyastāḥ śaṅkhaḥ satkamalāñjanam ..
pūrṇakumbhaṃ gajamadaṃ dūrvāḥ sārdraṃ ca gomayam .. 25 ..
1.177.d:
नद्यः काञ्चनविन्यस्ताः शङ्खः सत्कमलाञ्जनम् ॥
पूर्णकुम्भं गजमदं दूर्वाः सार्द्रं च गोमयम् ॥ 25 ॥
1.177.m:
[figures of] rivers fashioned in gold, a conch, fine lotuses, collyrium,
a full jar, elephant-rut, dūrvā grass, and fresh cow dung.

1.177.s:
ratnānyādāya bilvaṃ ca cāpamādāya satvaraḥ ..
saśaraṃ rāghavaśreṣṭhaḥ padadvātriṃśakaṃ yayau .. 26 ..
1.177.d:
रत्नान्यादाय बिल्वं च चापमादाय सत्वरः ॥
सशरं राघवश्रेष्ठः पदद्वात्रिंशकं ययौ ॥ 26 ॥
1.177.m:
Taking jewels and a bilva fruit, and swiftly grasping his bow
with arrows, the best of the Raghus advanced thirty-two paces.

1.177.s:
śreṣṭhamaśvaṃ sucandrābhaṃ hemabhāṇḍaparicchadam ..
āruhya niryayau śrīmāñjayakārābhipūjitaḥ .. 27 ..
1.177.d:
श्रेष्ठमश्वं सुचन्द्राभं हेमभाण्डपरिच्छदम् ॥
आरुह्य निर्ययौ श्रीमाञ्जयकाराभिपूजितः ॥ 27 ॥
1.177.m:
Mounting an excellent horse radiant as the clear moon,
adorned with golden accoutrements and trappings, the glorious one went forth, acclaimed with shouts of victory.

1.177.s:
paurajānapadāmātyairvādyaghoṣeṇa bhūriṇā ..
hrādena gajaghaṇṭānāṃ bṛṃhitena punaḥpunaḥ .. 28..
1.177.d:
पौरजानपदामात्यैर्वाद्यघोषेण भूरिणा ॥
ह्रादेन गजघण्टानां बृंहितेन पुनःपुनः ॥ 28॥
1.177.m:
Accompanied by citizens, country-folk, and ministers, by a great sound of musical instruments,
by the ringing of elephant bells, and repeated trumpeting,

1.177.s:
heṣitena turaṅgāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ kṣveḍitena ca ..
dvijapuṇyāhaghoṣeṇa prayāto bhūridakṣiṇaḥ .. 29 ..
1.177.d:
हेषितेन तुरङ्गाणां नराणां क्ष्वेडितेन च ॥
द्विजपुण्याहघोषेण प्रयातो भूरिदक्षिणः ॥ 29 ॥
1.177.m:
by the neighing of horses, the shouts of men,
and the sound of auspicious days declared by twice-borns, he departed, bountiful in sacrificial fees.

1.177.s:
bharatasya prayāṇe tu devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ ..
mumucuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi vāca ūcuḥ śubhāstathā .. 1.202.30 ..
1.177.d:
भरतस्य प्रयाणे तु देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः ॥
मुमुचुः पुष्पवर्षाणि वाच ऊचुः शुभास्तथा ॥ 1.202.30 ॥
1.177.m:
At Bharata's departure, however, the gods, headed by Śakra,
released showers of flowers and spoke auspicious words:

1.177.s:
eṣa vigrahavāndharma eṣa satyavatāṃ varaḥ ..
eṣa vīryavatāṃ śreṣṭho rūpeṇāpratimo bhuvi .. 31 ..
1.177.d:
एष विग्रहवान्धर्म एष सत्यवतां वरः ॥
एष वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठो रूपेणाप्रतिमो भुवि ॥ 31 ॥
1.177.m:
“He is dharma embodied; he is the foremost of the truthful;
he is the best among the mighty, incomparable on earth in beauty.

1.177.s:
anena yatkṛtaṃ karma rāme vanamupāgate ..
na tasya kartā loke'smindivi vā vidyate kvacit .. 32 ..
1.177.d:
अनेन यत्कृतं कर्म रामे वनमुपागते ॥
न तस्य कर्ता लोकेऽस्मिन्दिवि वा विद्यते क्वचित् ॥ 32 ॥
1.177.m:
The deed that was done by him when Rāma went to the forest—
no doer of such a deed exists anywhere in this world or in heaven.

1.177.s:
anena rājyaṃ santyaktaṃ gṛhaṃ dagdhamivāgninā ..
anena duḥkhaśayyāsu śayitaṃ samahātmanā .. 33 ..
1.177.d:
अनेन राज्यं सन्त्यक्तं गृहं दग्धमिवाग्निना ॥
अनेन दुःखशय्यासु शयितं समहात्मना ॥ 33 ॥
1.177.m:
By him the kingdom was abandoned, as if it were a house consumed by fire;
by him, the great-souled one, sleep was taken on painful beds.

1.177.s:
nityamāsannabhogena jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇā ..
phalamūlāśinānena rāmarājyaṃ hi pālitam .. 34 ..
1.177.d:
नित्यमासन्नभोगेन जटावल्कलधारिणा ॥
फलमूलाशिनानेन रामराज्यं हि पालितम् ॥ 34 ॥
1.177.m:
Having constantly kept pleasures at bay, wearing matted hair and bark garments,
eating roots and fruits, he indeed protected Rāma's kingdom.”

1.177.s:
śṛṇvansuvākyāni sureritāni rāmānujo rāmagṛhaṃ jagāma ..
śūrāryavidvatpuruṣopakīrṇaṃ ratnairyathā sāgaramaprameyam .. 35 ..
1.203
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
gṛhātprayāte bharate prasthānārthini yādava ..
prāgeva lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo nityodyuktamabhāṣata .. 1 ..
anuyānaṃ kumārasya bharatasya mahātmanaḥ ..
preṣayāśvasahasrāṇāṃ śatāni trīṇi rāghava .. 2 ..
daśa dantisahasrāṇi rathānāṃ ṣaḍguṇāni ca ..
koṭyaḥ pañca padātīnāṃ samareṣvanivartinām .. 3 ..
dhanādhyakṣāstathā vatsamanugacchantu lakṣmaṇa ..
gorathaiśca tathā puṣṭairgobhiruṣṭraistathaiva ca .. 4 ..
vyāyataiḥ puruṣairaśvairgardabhaiśca tathā varaiḥ ..
vastrarūpyasuvarṇānāṃ maṇīnāmapi bhāgaśaḥ .. 5 ..
visargāya kumārasya paripūrṇā yathāsukham ..
brāhmaṇāḥ kathayā mukhyāstathaiva naṭavartakāḥ .. 6 ..
1.177.d:
शृण्वन्सुवाक्यानि सुरेरितानि रामानुजो रामगृहं जगाम ॥
शूरार्यविद्वत्पुरुषोपकीर्णं रत्नैर्यथा सागरमप्रमेयम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.203
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
गृहात्प्रयाते भरते प्रस्थानार्थिनि यादव ॥
प्रागेव लक्ष्मणं रामो नित्योद्युक्तमभाषत ॥ 1 ॥
अनुयानं कुमारस्य भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥
प्रेषयाश्वसहस्राणां शतानि त्रीणि राघव ॥ 2 ॥
दश दन्तिसहस्राणि रथानां षड्गुणानि च ॥
कोट्यः पञ्च पदातीनां समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम् ॥ 3 ॥
धनाध्यक्षास्तथा वत्समनुगच्छन्तु लक्ष्मण ॥
गोरथैश्च तथा पुष्टैर्गोभिरुष्ट्रैस्तथैव च ॥ 4 ॥
व्यायतैः पुरुषैरश्वैर्गर्दभैश्च तथा वरैः ॥
वस्त्ररूप्यसुवर्णानां मणीनामपि भागशः ॥ 5 ॥
विसर्गाय कुमारस्य परिपूर्णा यथासुखम् ॥
ब्राह्मणाः कथया मुख्यास्तथैव नटवर्तकाः ॥ 6 ॥
1.177.m:
Hearing the fine words uttered by the gods, Rāma's younger brother went to Rāma's palace,
which was crowded with heroic, noble, and learned men, just as the unfathomable ocean is filled with jewels.
1.203
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When Bharata had set forth from his house, desirous of departure, O descendant of Yadu,
Rāma had already spoken beforehand to Lakṣmaṇa, who was ever ready:
“For the retinue of the great-souled prince Bharata,
send three hundred thousands of horses, O descendant of Raghu,
ten thousand tuskers, and six times that number of chariots,
and fifty million foot-soldiers who never turn back in battle.
Let the treasurers likewise follow the dear child, O Lakṣmaṇa,
with bullock carts, well-fed cattle, and camels,
with robust men, horses, and excellent donkeys,
[carrying] portions of textiles, silver, gold, and jewels,
abundant for the prince's distribution, at his pleasure.
Let brahmins pre-eminent in storytelling, as well as actors and dancers,

1.177.s:
gīte nṛtte tathā lāsye pravīṇāśca varāṅganāḥ ..
prāsthānikāśca ye kecitpānavikrayiṇaśca ye .. 7 ..
rūpājīvāśca vaṇijo nānāpaṇyopajīvinaḥ ..
nānārūpamupādāya bahupaṇyaṃ vrajantu vai..8..
viṣavaidyāḥ śalyavaidyāstathā kāyacikitsakāḥ ..
karmantikā sthapatayo mārgiṇo vṛkṣaropakāḥ .. 9 ..
kūpakārāḥ sudhākārā vaṃśakarmakṛtastathā ..
vāṇikkārāśca ye kecitkūrcakārāśca śobhanāḥ .. 1.203.10 ..
parikarmakṛtaścaiva tathā vastropajīvinaḥ ..
māyūrikāstaittirikāścetakā bhedakāśca ye .. 11 ..
rañjakā dantakārāśca tathā dantopajīvinaḥ ..
eraṇḍavetrakārāśca kaṭakārāśca śobhanāḥ .. 12 ..
ārakūṭakṛtaścaiva tātrakūṭāstathaiva ca ..
bhūrjakūṭāḥ khaḍgakārā guḍasīdhuprapācakāḥ .. 13 ..
aurabhrakā māhiṣakāstunnavāyāśca lakṣmaṇa ..
ye cābhiṣṭāvakāḥ kecitsūtamāgadhabandinaḥ .. 14 ..
1.177.d:
गीते नृत्ते तथा लास्ये प्रवीणाश्च वराङ्गनाः ॥
प्रास्थानिकाश्च ये केचित्पानविक्रयिणश्च ये ॥ 7 ॥
रूपाजीवाश्च वणिजो नानापण्योपजीविनः ॥
नानारूपमुपादाय बहुपण्यं व्रजन्तु वै॥8॥
विषवैद्याः शल्यवैद्यास्तथा कायचिकित्सकाः ॥
कर्मन्तिका स्थपतयो मार्गिणो वृक्षरोपकाः ॥ 9 ॥
कूपकाराः सुधाकारा वंशकर्मकृतस्तथा ॥
वाणिक्काराश्च ये केचित्कूर्चकाराश्च शोभनाः ॥ 1.203.10 ॥
परिकर्मकृतश्चैव तथा वस्त्रोपजीविनः ॥
मायूरिकास्तैत्तिरिकाश्चेतका भेदकाश्च ये ॥ 11 ॥
रञ्जका दन्तकाराश्च तथा दन्तोपजीविनः ॥
एरण्डवेत्रकाराश्च कटकाराश्च शोभनाः ॥ 12 ॥
आरकूटकृतश्चैव तात्रकूटास्तथैव च ॥
भूर्जकूटाः खड्गकारा गुडसीधुप्रपाचकाः ॥ 13 ॥
औरभ्रका माहिषकास्तुन्नवायाश्च लक्ष्मण ॥
ये चाभिष्टावकाः केचित्सूतमागधबन्दिनः ॥ 14 ॥
1.177.m:
excellent women skilled in singing, dancing, and gentle dance,
and whatever purveyors of provisions for the journey and liquor sellers there may be,
courtesans, and merchants living by various wares—
let them indeed go, taking with them abundant merchandise of various kinds.
Toxicologists, surgeons, and physicians of internal medicine,
manual workers, master builders, road-makers, and tree-planters,
well-diggers, whitewashers, and workers in bamboo,
arrow-makers, and excellent brush-makers,
attendants, and dealers in textiles,
peacock-catchers, partridge-catchers, hunters, and trappers,
dyers, ivory-carvers, and ivory-workers,
workers in castor and cane, and skilled mat-weavers,
brass-smiths, and likewise coppersmiths,
birch-bark processors, swordsmiths, and brewers of molasses rum,
shepherds, buffalo-keepers, and tailors, O Lakṣmaṇa,
and whatever panegyrists, bards, heralds, and minstrels,

1.177.s:
cailanirṇejakāścaiva carmakārāstathaiva ca ..
aṅgārakorāśca tathā lubdhakā ye ca dhīvarāḥ .. 15 ..
kabandhadhāriṇo ye ca ye ca kāṣṭhaprapāṭakāḥ ..
vastrasīvanasaktāśca gṛhakārāśca ye narāḥ .. 16 ..
kumbhakārāśca ye kecicchmaśruvardhakinaśca ye ..
lekhakā gaṇakā ye ca tathā tandulakārakāḥ .. 17 ..
saktukārāśca ye kecicchākapaṇyopajīvinaḥ ..
tailikā gāndhikāścaiva tīrthasaṃśuddhikārakāḥ ..16..
citrakarmavido ye ca ye ca lāṅgūlikā janāḥ ..

1.177.d:
चैलनिर्णेजकाश्चैव चर्मकारास्तथैव च ॥
अङ्गारकोराश्च तथा लुब्धका ये च धीवराः ॥ 15 ॥
कबन्धधारिणो ये च ये च काष्ठप्रपाटकाः ॥
वस्त्रसीवनसक्ताश्च गृहकाराश्च ये नराः ॥ 16 ॥
कुम्भकाराश्च ये केचिच्छ्मश्रुवर्धकिनश्च ये ॥
लेखका गणका ये च तथा तन्दुलकारकाः ॥ 17 ॥
सक्तुकाराश्च ये केचिच्छाकपण्योपजीविनः ॥
तैलिका गान्धिकाश्चैव तीर्थसंशुद्धिकारकाः ॥16॥
चित्रकर्मविदो ये च ये च लाङ्गूलिका जनाः ॥
सूताः पौरोगवाश्चैव सौविदल्लाश्च लक्ष्मण ॥ 19 ॥
गोपा वनचरा ये च नदीतीरविचारणाः ॥
गोसंघैर्महिषीसंघैस्तेऽनुयान्तु यथासुखम् ॥ 1.203.20 ॥
श्रेणीमहत्तरा ये च ग्रामघोषमहत्तराः ॥
तथैवाटविका ये च ये च शैलविचारिणः ॥ 21 ॥
सौमित्रे सर्व एवैते सुभृताश्च सुपूजिताः ॥
अनुयान्तु कुमारं मे भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्॥ 22 ॥
1.177.m:
washermen, and likewise leatherworkers,
charcoal-burners, hunters, and fishermen,
water-carriers, and wood-cutters,
men engaged in sewing clothes, and house-builders,
potters, and barbers,
scribes, accountants, and grain-pounders,
makers of parched-grain flour, and green-grocers,
oil-pressers, perfumers, and inspectors of ford crossings,
those skilled in painting, and tail-fan makers,
charioteers, cooks, and palace chamberlains, O Lakṣmaṇa,
cowherds, forest-dwellers, and those wandering riverbanks—
let them follow comfortably with herds of cattle and herds of buffaloes.
The leaders of artisan guilds, and the headmen of villages and pastoral settlements,
as well as foresters, and mountain-dwellers—
O son of Sumitrā, let all these, well-provided and well-honoured,
follow my prince Bharata, who is devoted to his brothers.”

1.177.d:
इत्येवमुक्तः स तु तान्समस्तानाज्ञापयामास नरेन्द्रवाक्यात् ॥
आमन्त्र्य रामं शिरसा च सर्वे विनिर्ययुस्ते नगरात्प्रहृष्टाः ॥23॥
1.204
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रामः शुश्राव तन्महत्॥
शङ्खवाद्यरवोन्मिश्रं भरतस्यानुयात्रिकम् ॥ 1 ॥
राजद्वारमुपागत्य भरतोऽपि महायशाः ॥
पदभ्यां जगाम राजानमवतीर्य तुरङ्गमात्॥2॥
स ददर्श तदा रामं रत्नसिंहासनस्थितम्॥
अनुलिप्तं परार्ध्येन चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना॥3॥
सूक्ष्मं वसानं वसनं सर्वाभरणभूषितम॥
तेजसा भास्कराकारं सौन्दर्येणोडुपोपमम् ॥ 4 ॥
क्षमया पृथिवीतुल्यं क्रोधे कालानलोपमम् ॥
बृहस्पतिसमं बुद्ध्या विष्णुतुल्यं पराक्रमे ॥5॥
सत्ये दानेऽप्यनौपम्यं दमे शीले च राघवम् ॥
पुरोहितैरमात्यैश्च युतं प्रकृतिभिस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥
1.177.m:
Thus addressed, he commanded all of them according to the king's word;
and having bowed their heads in leave-taking to Rāma, they all departed joyful from the city.
1.204
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
At that very time, Rāma heard that great
retinue of Bharata, mingled with the sound of conches and musical instruments.
Having arrived at the royal gate, the highly renowned Bharata
dismounted from his horse and went on foot to the king.
He then saw Rāma seated on a jewel-adorned lion throne,
anointed with supreme, fragrant sandalwood paste,
wearing fine garments, adorned with all ornaments,
resembling the sun in radiance and the moon in beauty.
equal to the earth in forbearance, like the fire of time in wrath, / equal to Bṛhaspati in intellect, like Viṣṇu in valour,
unmatched in truth and generosity, and in self-restraint and virtue, the descendant of Raghu, / accompanied by his family priests, ministers, and subjects.

1.177.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं भरतः श्रीमाञ्जगाम शिरसा महीम् ॥
भरतं युवराजानं रामाय विदितात्मने ॥ 7 ॥
न्यवेदयत धर्मात्मा प्रतीहारः सलक्ष्मणम् ॥
उत्थाय कण्ठे जग्राह रामोऽपि भरतं तदा ॥ 8 ॥
मूर्ध्नि चैनमुपाघ्राय आदिदेशास्य शासनम् ॥
भरतं तु सुखासीनं रामो वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 9 ॥
गन्धर्वपुत्रांस्तान्हत्वा कर्तव्यं नगरद्वयम् ॥
सिन्धो रुभयपार्श्वे तु पुत्रयोरुभयोः कृते ॥ 1.204.10 ॥
अभिषिच्य तदा वत्स पुत्रौ नगरयोस्तयोः ॥
युधाजिति परीधाय क्षिप्रमागन्तुमर्हसि ॥11॥
त्वया विना नरव्याघ्र नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे ॥
क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य तत्र त्वं प्रेषितो मया ॥12॥
स त्वं गच्छ महाभाग मा ते कालात्ययो भवेत् ॥
स्वस्त्यस्तु तेन्तरिक्षेभ्यः पार्थिवेभ्यश्च गच्छतः ॥ 13 ॥
दिव्येभ्यश्चैव भूतेभ्यः समरे च तथानघ ॥ 14 ॥
1.177.m:
Seeing him, glorious Bharata bowed down his head to the ground. / Bharata the crown prince, along with Lakṣmaṇa, to Rāma who knew his own self,
the righteous doorkeeper announced. / Rising, Rāma too then embraced Bharata around the neck,
and smelling him on the head, he commanded his orders. / And to Bharata seated comfortably, Rāma spoke these words:
"Having slain those sons of the Gandharva, two cities must be built / on both sides of the Sindhu for both your sons.
Having consecrated your two sons in those two cities, my dear child, / and having entrusted them to Yudhājit, you must return quickly.
Without you, tiger among men, I have no desire to live; / placing the duty of a kṣatriya foremost, you are sent there by me.
Go, therefore, fortunate one; let there be no delay for you. / May there be welfare for you as you travel, from airborne and earthly beings,
and from divine beings, and likewise in battle, sinless one!

1.177.d:
स्वांस्वां दिशमधिष्ठाय दिक्पाला दीप्ततेजसः ॥
पालयन्तु सदा तुभ्यं दीप्तविग्रहधारिणः ॥ 15 ॥
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च साध्याश्च समरुद्गणाः ॥
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा अश्विनौ च भिषग्वरौ ॥ 16 ॥
भृगवोङ्गिरसश्चैव कालस्यावयवास्तथा ॥
सरितः सागराः शैलाः समुद्राश्च सरांसि च ॥ 17 ॥
दैत्यदानवगन्धर्वा पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः ॥
देवपत्न्यस्तथा सर्वा देवमातर एव च ॥ 18 ॥
शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि शास्त्राणि मङ्गलाय भवन्तु ते ॥
विजयं दीर्घमायुश्च भोगांश्चान्यान्दिशन्तु ते ॥ 19 ॥
इति स्वस्त्ययनं श्रुत्वा राज्ञा स समुदीरितम् ॥
रामस्य पादौ शिरसा त्वभिवन्द्य धनुर्धरः ॥ 1.204.20 ॥
निर्गत्य राजभवनाद्रामाज्ञाकल्पितं जगत ॥
हिमाद्रिकूटसंकाशं चारुदंष्ट्रोज्ज्वलाननम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.177.m:
Taking their stand each in his own quarter, may the guardians of the directions of blazing splendour, / bearing radiant forms, protect you at all times!
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, the Sādhyas along with the hosts of Maruts, / the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, and the two Aśvins, best of physicians,
the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases, and the divisions of time, / rivers, oceans, mountains, seas, and lakes,
Daityas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, / and all the wives of the gods, and the mothers of the gods—
may weapons, missiles, and sciences be for your auspiciousness; / may they grant you victory, long life, and other pleasures!"
Having heard this blessing of auspicious journey uttered by the king, / bowing with his head at Rāma's feet, that archer,
departing from the royal palace, [mounted the elephant] prepared by Rāma's command: / resembling a peak of the snowy mountain, with beautiful tusks and a radiant face,

1.177.d:
मदेन सिञ्चमानं च नृपवेश्माजिरं नृप ॥
समाक्रान्तकटं चापि पानलुब्धशिलीमुखैः ॥ 22 ॥
स्तब्धचारुमहाकर्णं मधुपकृपयैव तु ॥
दीर्घाग्रमध्वक्षकृतं कृतशृङ्गावतंसकम् ॥ 23 ॥
स्वासनं व्यूढकुम्भं च तथोदग्रं महाबलम् ॥
नक्षत्रमालां शिरसा धारयानं तु काञ्चनीम् ॥ 24 ॥
पटुस्वने तथा घण्टे दर्शनीये मनोहरे ॥
कुथं विचित्रं रम्यं च कोविदारं महाध्वजं ॥ 25 ॥
वैजयन्त्यः पताकाश्च किङ्किणीजालमालिताः ॥
समारूढं नयविदा महामात्रेण धीमता ॥ 26 ॥
वैडूर्यदण्डतीक्ष्णाग्र काञ्चनाङ्कुशधारिणा ॥
जघनस्थेन चान्येन वरतोमरधारिणा ॥ 27 ॥
तथा वैजयिकैर्मन्त्रैर्देवज्ञेनाभिमन्त्रितम् ॥
आरुरोह महातेजा जयत्काराभिनन्दिनः ॥28॥
पूर्णेन्दुमण्डलाकारं रुक्मदण्डं मनोहरम् ॥
छत्रमादाय तं प्रेम्णा चारुरोह स लक्ष्मणः ॥ 29 ॥
1.177.m:
sprinkling the courtyard of the king's palace with rutting fluid, O king, / its temples swarmed by bees greedy to drink,
with motionlessly held, beautiful, large ears out of pity for the bees, / with the long tip of its trunk active along the way, decorated with peaked ornaments,
with a good seat, broad frontal lobes, towering, and of great strength, / bearing on its head a golden necklace of twenty-seven pearls,
with two sharp-sounding, lovely, and enchanting bells, / with a variegated and pleasing housing, and a great banner of the kovidāra tree,
with victory banners and pennants encircled by nets of small bells, / mounted by a wise mahout versed in polity,
holding a golden goad with a sharp point and a staff of cat's-eye gem, / and with another man seated behind holding an excellent lance,
consecrated by the astrologer with mantras of victory, / the exceedingly splendid one mounted, welcomed with cries of 'Victory!'
Taking a charming umbrella shaped like the disc of the full moon / with a golden staff, Lakṣmaṇa mounted it out of affection.

चामरौ द्वौ समादाय चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभौ ॥
आरूढं योषितोर्युग्मं रूपेणाऽप्रतिमं भुवि ॥ 1.204.30 ॥
तं समारुह्य नागेन्द्रं मदलेखाभिगामिनम् ॥
जगाम सह गार्ग्येण रथारूढेन यादव ॥ 31 ॥

तूर्यघोषेण महता बन्दिनां निःस्वनेन च ॥ 34 ॥
वायुना चानुलोमेन सेव्यमानः सुगन्धिना ॥ ।
मङ्गलानां च मुख्यानां दर्शनाद्धृष्टमानसः ॥ 39 ॥
1.177.m:
Taking two chowries radiant as rays of the moon, / a pair of women of peerless beauty on earth mounted.
Having mounted that lord of elephants following the trail of rut, / he set out, O Yādava, together with Gārgya mounted on a chariot.
A great fourfold army followed him, O fortunate one, / crowded with pennants and banners, shaking the earth.
Hawks, crows, herons, Piśācas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas / went ahead of that great-souled Bharata,
greedy for the flesh of the Gandharva's sons, living on meat. / With the loud blast of horns and the sound of bards,
served by a favourable, fragrant breeze, / his heart gladdened by the sight of foremost auspicious omens,

1.177.s:
niryayau rājamārgeṇa janasambādhaśālinā ..
tejasvināṃ ca tejāṃsi hṛdayāni ca yoṣi tām .. 36 ..
1.177.d:
निर्ययौ राजमार्गेण जनसम्बाधशालिना ॥
तेजस्विनां च तेजांसि हृदयानि च योषि ताम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.177.m: he set forth along the royal road crowded with people, / taking away the splendour of the splendid and the hearts of women.

1.177.s:
ādadāno mahātejā nagarātsa viniryayau ..
krośamātraṃ tato gatvā same deśe ca sodake .. 37 ..
1.177.d:
आददानो महातेजा नगरात्स विनिर्ययौ ॥
क्रोशमात्रं ततो गत्वा समे देशे च सोदके ॥ 37 ॥
1.177.m: Possessing great splendour, he set out from the city. / Having then travelled a distance of one krośa to a level place with water,

1.177.s:
praśastadrumasaṃkīrṇe śibiraṃ prāṅniṣevitam ..
senādhyakṣaiḥ sunipuṇairviveśa bharatastadā .. 38 ..
1.177.d:
प्रशस्तद्रुमसंकीर्णे शिबिरं प्राङ्निषेवितम् ॥
सेनाध्यक्षैः सुनिपुणैर्विवेश भरतस्तदा ॥ 38 ॥
1.177.m: thick with auspicious trees, Bharata then entered the camp / previously prepared by skilful commanders of the army.

1.177.s:
sa praviśya mahātejāḥ śibiraṃ svaṃ niveśanam ..
maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā varāsanagataḥ prabhuḥ .. 39 ..
1.177.d:
स प्रविश्य महातेजाः शिबिरं स्वं निवेशनम् ॥
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा वरासनगतः प्रभुः ॥ 39 ॥
1.177.m: Entering the camp, his own dwelling, / having performed the touching of auspicious items, the lord, seated on an excellent throne,

1.177.s:
paurajānapadaṃ sarvaṃ preṣayāmāsa yādava ..
pariṣvajya tataḥ paścāllakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam .. 1.204.40 ..
1.177.d:
पौरजानपदं सर्वं प्रेषयामास यादव ॥
परिष्वज्य ततः पश्चाल्लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम् ॥ 1.204.40 ॥
1.177.m: sent back all the citizens and countryfolk, O Yādava. / Then, having embraced Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks,

1.177.s:
mūrdhni caivamupāghrāya preṣayāmāsa dharmavit ..
prāyāṇakaṃ ca śvobhūte dundubhistāḍyatāṃ mama .. 41 ..
1.177.d:
मूर्ध्नि चैवमुपाघ्राय प्रेषयामास धर्मवित् ॥
प्रायाणकं च श्वोभूते दुन्दुभिस्ताड्यतां मम ॥ 41 ॥
1.177.m: and smelling him on the head, the knower of dharma sent him back: / "Tomorrow, let my march-drum be beaten!

1.177.s:
daiśikāḥ purato yāntu ye ca vṛkṣāvarohakāḥ ..
ājñāpya sakalaṃ caiva śibiraṃ ca tathāvidham .. 42 ..
1.177.d:
दैशिकाः पुरतो यान्तु ये च वृक्षावरोहकाः ॥
आज्ञाप्य सकलं चैव शिबिरं च तथाविधम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.177.m: Let guides go in front, as well as tree-clearers!" / Having commanded the entire camp in this manner:

1.177.s:
avṛkṣeṣu tu deśeṣu ropayantu drumāñjanāḥ ..
drumāḥ kaṇṭakinaścaiva ye ca mārgaprarodhakāḥ .. 43 ..
1.177.d:
अवृक्षेषु तु देशेषु रोपयन्तु द्रुमाञ्जनाः ॥
द्रुमाः कण्टकिनश्चैव ये च मार्गप्ररोधकाः ॥ 43 ॥
1.177.m: "In treeless places, let people plant trees; / and the thorny trees that block the road,

1.177.s:
chindantu gatvā tānadya tīkṣṇaiḥ śīghraṃ paraśvadhaiḥ ..
toyahīneṣu deśeṣu kūpānkurvantu me tathā .. 44 ..
1.177.d:
छिन्दन्तु गत्वा तानद्य तीक्ष्णैः शीघ्रं परश्वधैः ॥
तोयहीनेषु देशेषु कूपान्कुर्वन्तु मे तथा ॥ 44 ॥
1.177.m: let them go and quickly cut them down today with sharp axes; / in waterless regions, let them likewise dig wells for me;

1.177.s:
viṣamāṃśca tathā deśānsamānkurvantu me pathi ..
tīrāṇi saritāṃ caiva kurvantu pulināni ca .. 45 ..
1.177.d:
विषमांश्च तथा देशान्समान्कुर्वन्तु मे पथि ॥
तीराणि सरितां चैव कुर्वन्तु पुलिनानि च ॥ 45 ॥
1.177.m: and let them level the uneven places on my path; / and let them make banks and sandbars for the rivers,

1.177.s:
na bhavedyena saṃghaṭṭo janasya pathi yāsyataḥ ..
puraḥ prayāntu sainyena vijaye rativardhanāḥ .. 46 ..
1.177.d:
न भवेद्येन संघट्टो जनस्य पथि यास्यतः ॥
पुरः प्रयान्तु सैन्येन विजये रतिवर्धनाः ॥ 46 ॥
1.177.m: so that there will be no crush among the people travelling on the road. / Let those who increase delight in victory advance in front with the army:

1.177.s:
nīlaśca nakradevaśca vasumānmunayastathā ..
madhyaprayāṇe gāndhāro jayanābho raṇotkaṭaḥ .. 47 ..
1.177.d:
नीलश्च नक्रदेवश्च वसुमान्मुनयस्तथा ॥
मध्यप्रयाणे गान्धारो जयनाभो रणोत्कटः ॥ 47 ॥
1.177.m: Nīla, Nakradeva, Vasumat, and the Munis; / in the centre of the march, Gāndhāra, Jayanābha, ferocious in battle,

1.177.s:
suśīlaḥ kāmapālaśca yāntu sainyena daṃśitāḥ ..
jaghanaṃ kaṭakasyāhaṃ pālayāno yathāsukham .. 48 ..
1.177.d:
सुशीलः कामपालश्च यान्तु सैन्येन दंशिताः ॥
जघनं कटकस्याहं पालयानो यथासुखम् ॥ 48 ॥
1.177.m: Suśīla, and Kāmapāla—armoured with their troops, let them march. / Protecting the rear of the camp at my ease,

1.177.s:
sainyena saha yāsyāmi vijayāya nṛpasya tu ..
paśyantu daiśikāḥ sthānaṃ prabhūtayavasendhanam .. .. 49 ..
1.177.d:
सैन्येन सह यास्यामि विजयाय नृपस्य तु ॥
पश्यन्तु दैशिकाः स्थानं प्रभूतयवसेन्धनम् ॥ ॥ 49 ॥
1.177.m: I shall march with the army for the king's victory. / Let the guides seek out a site with abundant grass and firewood."

1.177.s:
sodakaṃ ca samaṃ yatra senāvāso bhavenmama ..
evamājñāpya bharato vijahāra yathāsukham .. 1.204.50 ..
1.177.d:
सोदकं च समं यत्र सेनावासो भवेन्मम ॥
एवमाज्ञाप्य भरतो विजहार यथासुखम् ॥ 1.204.50 ॥
1.177.m: [Let the guides find a place] with water and level ground, where the encampment of my army may be.” / Having thus commanded, Bharata took his recreation at his ease.

1.177.s: suṣvāpa ca niśāṃ tatra gharmakāle manoharām ..51..
1.177.d: सुष्वाप च निशां तत्र घर्मकाले मनोहराम् ॥51॥
1.177.m: And he slept there through the night, charming in the hot season.

1.177.s:
suptasya sā tatra raghūdvahasya puṇyā yayau rātriradīnasattvā ..
sampūrṇacandrābharaṇā pratītā jyeṣṭhasya māsasya raṇotsukasya .. 52..
1.205
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ dundubhiḥ samahanyata ..
prayāṇiko mahārāja bharatasya mahāsvanaḥ .. 1 ..
tasya śabdena mahatā vibuddhaḥ kaṭake janaḥ ..
avaśyakaraṇīyāni kṛtvā rājaṃstvarānvitāḥ .. 2 ..
tvaritā gamanārthāya samāhūyetaretaram ..
paṭaveśmāni ramyāṇi sahantumupacakramuḥ .. 3 ..
mahānti sumanojñāni vartitorṇākṛtāni ca ..
cakrustāni ca rājendra sukhavāhyānyayatnataḥ .. 4 ..
tatastvāropayāñcakruḥ karabheṣu khareṣu ca ..
goratheṣu tu mukhyeṣu tathā dantiṣu satvarāḥ .. 5 ..
bhāṇḍamuccāvacaṃ caiva śayanāni mṛdūni ca ..
āsanāni ca mukhyāni bhāṇḍaṃ yacca mahānase .. 6 ..
1.177.d:
सुप्तस्य सा तत्र रघूद्वहस्य पुण्या ययौ रात्रिरदीनसत्त्वा ॥
सम्पूर्णचन्द्राभरणा प्रतीता ज्येष्ठस्य मासस्य रणोत्सुकस्य ॥ 52॥
1.205
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां दुन्दुभिः समहन्यत ॥
प्रयाणिको महाराज भरतस्य महास्वनः ॥ 1 ॥
तस्य शब्देन महता विबुद्धः कटके जनः ॥
अवश्यकरणीयानि कृत्वा राजंस्त्वरान्विताः ॥ 2 ॥
त्वरिता गमनार्थाय समाहूयेतरेतरम् ॥
पटवेश्मानि रम्याणि सहन्तुमुपचक्रमुः ॥ 3 ॥
महान्ति सुमनोज्ञानि वर्तितोर्णाकृतानि च ॥
चक्रुस्तानि च राजेन्द्र सुखवाह्यान्ययत्नतः ॥ 4 ॥
ततस्त्वारोपयाञ्चक्रुः करभेषु खरेषु च ॥
गोरथेषु तु मुख्येषु तथा दन्तिषु सत्वराः ॥ 5 ॥
भाण्डमुच्चावचं चैव शयनानि मृदूनि च ॥
आसनानि च मुख्यानि भाण्डं यच्च महानसे ॥ 6 ॥
1.177.m:
As he, the scion of Raghu who was eager for battle, lay asleep, / there passed that auspicious night of resolute nature in the month of Jyeṣṭha, adorned with the full moon, renowned.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / But when the night had dawned, O great king, / the loud-sounding marching kettledrum of Bharata was struck.
Awakened by its great sound, the people in the camp, / having performed the necessary duties, filled with haste, O king,
hastening for the march, calling out to one another, / began to strike down the charming cloth-tents.
Large and very pleasing, made of spun wool, / they made them easily portable without effort, O best of kings.
Then with all speed they loaded upon young camels, donkeys, / excellent bullock-carts, and likewise upon elephants,
baggage of various kinds, soft beds, / excellent seats, and whatever utensils were in the kitchen,

1.177.s:
peyaṃ ca yavasaṃ caiva śastrāṇi vividhāni ca ..
kavacāni turaṅgāṇāṃ śilpabhāṇḍāni yāni ca .. 7 ..
dhanaṃ ca vividhaṃ rājansarvopa karaṇāni ca ..
āropyamāṇe bhāṇḍe tu karabhāṇāṃ vikṛṣyatām .. 8 ..
śuśruve tumulaḥ śabdaḥ kharāṇāṃ ca kharasvanaḥ ..
gajānāṃ yujyamānānāṃ turaṅgāṇāṃ rathaiḥ saha .. 9 ..
vādyānāṃ hanyamānānāṃ śuśruve tumulaṃ svanam ..
nādena gajaghaṇṭānāṃ bṛṃhitena ca pārthiva .. 1.205.10 ..
hreṣitena turaṅgāṇāṃ babhūva tumulaḥ svanaḥ ..
prāyāṇikamupādāya tāḍayanneva dundubhim .. 11 ..
agre prayāṇamānyena yayau dundubhibhiḥ saha ..
paṇyāni ca samādāya vaṇijastvaritā yayuḥ .. 12 ..
grahītukāmāścānyāni sodakāni samāni ca ..
sthānāni varamukhyānāṃ yayuścāgresarā narāḥ .. 13 ..
mahānasikamukhyāstu tvaritāśca tathā yayuḥ ..
sukhayānāsu ramyāsu tathaivāśvatarīṣu ca .. 14 ..
1.177.d:
पेयं च यवसं चैव शस्त्राणि विविधानि च ॥
कवचानि तुरङ्गाणां शिल्पभाण्डानि यानि च ॥ 7 ॥
धनं च विविधं राजन्सर्वोप करणानि च ॥
आरोप्यमाणे भाण्डे तु करभाणां विकृष्यताम् ॥ 8 ॥
शुश्रुवे तुमुलः शब्दः खराणां च खरस्वनः ॥
गजानां युज्यमानानां तुरङ्गाणां रथैः सह ॥ 9 ॥
वाद्यानां हन्यमानानां शुश्रुवे तुमुलं स्वनम् ॥
नादेन गजघण्टानां बृंहितेन च पार्थिव ॥ 1.205.10 ॥
ह्रेषितेन तुरङ्गाणां बभूव तुमुलः स्वनः ॥
प्रायाणिकमुपादाय ताडयन्नेव दुन्दुभिम् ॥ 11 ॥
अग्रे प्रयाणमान्येन ययौ दुन्दुभिभिः सह ॥
पण्यानि च समादाय वणिजस्त्वरिता ययुः ॥ 12 ॥
ग्रहीतुकामाश्चान्यानि सोदकानि समानि च ॥
स्थानानि वरमुख्यानां ययुश्चाग्रेसरा नराः ॥ 13 ॥
महानसिकमुख्यास्तु त्वरिताश्च तथा ययुः ॥
सुखयानासु रम्यासु तथैवाश्वतरीषु च ॥ 14 ॥
1.177.m:
and drink, fodder, various weapons, / armours for the horses, and artisans' tools,
wealth of various kinds, O king, and all equipment. / As the baggage was being loaded, from the camels being dragged along,
a tumultuous noise was heard, and the harsh braying of donkeys; / from the elephants and horses being yoked to the chariots,
and from the musical instruments being beaten, a tumultuous sound was heard; / with the ringing of the elephant-bells and their trumpeting, O ruler of the earth,
and with the neighing of the horses, a tumultuous noise arose. / Striking the marching kettledrum,
one went ahead in front along with the kettledrums; / and the merchants set out swiftly, taking their wares.
Desiring to secure other level sites with water / for the foremost chiefs, the scouts went forward.
The chief cooks likewise set out swiftly; / and mounting the women on comfortable, charming conveyances

1.177.s:
āropya yoṣito jagmuḥ pratyūṣe muditā janāḥ ..
ārūḍhāścāparā nāryaḥ savitānāḥ kareṇavaḥ ..15..
kañcukoṣṇīṣibhirguptā guptā varṣavaraistathā ..
yayuḥ sasainyā rājendra gītavādya purassarāḥ .. 16 ..
dīnāndhakṛpaṇānāthāṃstarpayantyo dhanena tāḥ ..
narendrayoṣito rājñāṃ divyālaṅgārabhūṣitāḥ .. 17 ..
tathānye baddhanistriṃśāḥ puruṣāśca kalāpinaḥ ..
ādīpya tṛṇaveśmāni jagmustvaritamānasāḥ .. 18 ..
bharato'pi samāruhya śibikāṃ ratnabhūṣitām ..
viniryayau mahātejā stūryaghoṣapuraḥsaraḥ .. 19 ..
śūnyaṃ ca śibirasthānaṃ gṛdhramaṇḍalasaṃkulam ..
bahukravyādasaṅkīrṇaṃ kṣaṇena samapadyata .. 1.205.20 ..
gajoṣṭragardabhāśvānāṃ śarīrāvayavairyutam..
bhagnabhāṇḍasamākīrṇaṃ śarīrāvayavairyutam..21..
bahukravyādasaṅkīrṇaṃ karīṣotkarasaṃyutam ..
khātairmahānasasthānairdagdhamṛttikayā yutaiḥ .. ...22..
1.177.d:
आरोप्य योषितो जग्मुः प्रत्यूषे मुदिता जनाः ॥
आरूढाश्चापरा नार्यः सवितानाः करेणवः ॥15॥
कञ्चुकोष्णीषिभिर्गुप्ता गुप्ता वर्षवरैस्तथा ॥
ययुः ससैन्या राजेन्द्र गीतवाद्य पुरस्सराः ॥ 16 ॥
दीनान्धकृपणानाथांस्तर्पयन्त्यो धनेन ताः ॥
नरेन्द्रयोषितो राज्ञां दिव्यालङ्गारभूषिताः ॥ 17 ॥
तथान्ये बद्धनिस्त्रिंशाः पुरुषाश्च कलापिनः ॥
आदीप्य तृणवेश्मानि जग्मुस्त्वरितमानसाः ॥ 18 ॥
भरतोऽपि समारुह्य शिबिकां रत्नभूषिताम् ॥
विनिर्ययौ महातेजा स्तूर्यघोषपुरःसरः ॥ 19 ॥
शून्यं च शिबिरस्थानं गृध्रमण्डलसंकुलम् ॥
बहुक्रव्यादसङ्कीर्णं क्षणेन समपद्यत ॥ 1.205.20 ॥
गजोष्ट्रगर्दभाश्वानां शरीरावयवैर्युतम्॥
भग्नभाण्डसमाकीर्णं शरीरावयवैर्युतम्॥21॥
बहुक्रव्यादसङ्कीर्णं करीषोत्करसंयुतम् ॥
खातैर्महानसस्थानैर्दग्धमृत्तिकया युतैः ॥ ॥.22॥
1.177.m:
and likewise on she-mules, the delighted people went forth at dawn. / Other women mounted female elephants equipped with canopies;
protected by guards wearing coats and turbans, and protected by eunuchs, / accompanied by their troops, preceded by vocal and instrumental music, they marched, O best of kings.
Gratifying the poor, the blind, the miserable, and the helpless with wealth, / those wives of the lord of men and of kings were adorned with celestial ornaments.
Likewise other men, with swords girt and carrying quivers, / setting fire to the grass huts, set forth with hasty minds.
Bharata too, of great splendour, having mounted a palanquin adorned with jewels, / went forth, preceded by the sound of musical instruments.
And the vacated camp-site in an instant became filled with circles of vultures / and crowded with many flesh-eating beasts,
strewn with body-parts of elephants, camels, donkeys, and horses, / covered with broken pots, strewn with body-parts,
crowded with many flesh-eating beasts, littered with heaps of dung, / marked with pits for the kitchens containing burnt earth,

1.177.s:
samaṇḍakardamopetairmakṣikāsahitairyutam ..
saṃtyajya niryayuḥ sarve bharatasya tu sainikāḥ..23..

nāgānutthāpayāmāsurupaviṣṭānprayatnataḥ ..24..

1.177.d:
समण्डकर्दमोपेतैर्मक्षिकासहितैर्युतम् ॥
संत्यज्य निर्ययुः सर्वे भरतस्य तु सैनिकाः॥23॥
प्रयाणे तस्य सैन्यस्य बलीवर्दाञ्छ्रमान्वितान् ॥
नागानुत्थापयामासुरुपविष्टान्प्रयत्नतः ॥24॥
केचिदुष्ट्रपरित्रस्तातान्गार्दभेन निपातितान् ॥
भाण्डमारोपयाञ्चक्रुर्भूय एव नरोत्तमाः ॥ 25 ॥
नद्युत्तारेषु महिषान्केचित्सूर्यांशुतापितान् ॥
निषण्णान्सह भारेण ताडयाञ्चक्रिरे जनाः ॥ 26 ॥
केचिदश्वतरांस्त्रस्तान्नागबृंहितनिस्वनैः ॥
आरूढयोषितो यत्नाज्जगृहुर्नृप रश्मिषु ॥ 27 ॥
केचिदश्वैर्गजत्रस्तैराक्षिप्ता भुवि मानवाः ॥
जानुविश्रमणार्थाय वाजिग्रीवकृताङघ्रयः ॥ 28 ॥
तुरङ्गांश्च तदोद्भ्रान्तान्स्रस्तचर्माश्च सादिनः ॥
केचिदाक्रम्य वेगेन जगृहुस्तत्र यादव ॥ 29 ॥
विशश्रमुस्तथा केचिद्वृक्षच्छायासु मानवाः ॥
केचिच्चोदकतीरेषु चक्रिरे भोजनक्रियाम् ॥ 1.205.30 ॥
1.177.m:
filled with scum, mud, and flies; / leaving it behind, all the soldiers of Bharata departed.
During the march of that army, [the drivers] with great effort made the bullocks, / overcome with exhaustion, and the seated elephants rise up.
The best of men loaded baggage again on those [beasts] / that had been frightened by camels and thrown down by a donkey.
At river-crossings, people beat the buffaloes, / scorched by the sun's rays, that had sat down along with their loads.
Some, O king, carefully seized by the reins the mules / on which women were mounted, frightened by the trumpeting sounds of elephants.
Some men were thrown to the ground by horses terrified of elephants, / their feet resting on the horse's neck to rest their knees.
And riders whose shields had slipped swiftly overtook and seized / the horses that were then running wild, O Yādava.
Some men rested in the shade of trees, / while others took their meal on the banks of waters.

1.177.s:
kecitsantrastaturagasannikṛṣṭasamutthitaiḥ ..
drutānkāpiñjalairyatnājjagṛhustāṃsturaṅgamān .. 31 ..
kecitkaṭakasaṃtrastānmṛgayūthānpradhāvataḥ ..
vegenākramya viśikhairjaghnuryadukulodvaha .. 32 ..
kecicca yavasaṃ cakruḥ keciccakrurathendhanam ..
tathānyairdviguṇībhūtaṃ tathā dundubhinisvanam .. 33 ..
prāyāṇikaṃ jahuḥ śīghraṃ śramaṃ yadukulodvaha ..
kecidāpaṇavīthyagramahāvaṃśasamucchritam ..34 ..
sapatākaṃ narā dṛṣṭvā prāptāḥ sma iti menire ..
cakruḥ kecicca cchandāṃsi sahāyānāṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..35 ..
purogatānāṃ rājendra sthānalabdhicikīrṣayā ..
kecitpaṭakuṭīṃ dṛṣṭvā svakīyāṃ tvaritā yayuḥ .. 36 ..
vartitorṇākṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhāṃścānye yayurdrutam ..
keṣāñcittatra veśmāni tīrṇāni nṛpasattama .. 37 ..
1.177.d:
केचित्सन्त्रस्ततुरगसन्निकृष्टसमुत्थितैः ॥
द्रुतान्कापिञ्जलैर्यत्नाज्जगृहुस्तांस्तुरङ्गमान् ॥ 31 ॥
केचित्कटकसंत्रस्तान्मृगयूथान्प्रधावतः ॥
वेगेनाक्रम्य विशिखैर्जघ्नुर्यदुकुलोद्वह ॥ 32 ॥
केचिच्च यवसं चक्रुः केचिच्चक्रुरथेन्धनम् ॥
तथान्यैर्द्विगुणीभूतं तथा दुन्दुभिनिस्वनम् ॥ 33 ॥
प्रायाणिकं जहुः शीघ्रं श्रमं यदुकुलोद्वह ॥
केचिदापणवीथ्यग्रमहावंशसमुच्छ्रितम् ॥34 ॥
सपताकं नरा दृष्ट्वा प्राप्ताः स्म इति मेनिरे ॥
चक्रुः केचिच्च च्छन्दांसि सहायानां पुनःपुनः ॥35 ॥
पुरोगतानां राजेन्द्र स्थानलब्धिचिकीर्षया ॥
केचित्पटकुटीं दृष्ट्वा स्वकीयां त्वरिता ययुः ॥ 36 ॥
वर्तितोर्णाकृतं दृष्ट्वा गृहांश्चान्ये ययुर्द्रुतम् ॥
केषाञ्चित्तत्र वेश्मानि तीर्णानि नृपसत्तम ॥ 37 ॥
1.177.m:
Some carefully seized the horses that had bolted / on account of francolins rising close by, which terrified the horses.
Some, swiftly charging with arrows, slew the herds of deer / that were running away in fright from the camp, O scion of the Yadu clan.
Some gathered fodder, while others gathered firewood. / And doubled by the others, the sound of the marching kettledrum
quickly dispelled their fatigue, O scion of the Yadu clan. / Some men, seeing raised on a great bamboo pole the top of a market street
bearing a flag, thought, “We have arrived!” / Some repeatedly yielded to the wishes of their companions
who had gone ahead, O best of kings, desiring to secure a site. / Seeing their own cloth-tent, some went swiftly;
seeing the dwellings made of spun wool, others hurried on. / The residences of some there were already completed, O best of kings;

1.177.s:
kṛtāni kriyamāṇāni dadṛśustatra mānavāḥ ..
drumairviśrāmyamāṇaiśca kriyamāṇaistathā kaṭaiḥ .. 38 ..
gṛhairāropyamāṇaiśca paṭorṇātṛṇasaṃskṛtaiḥ ..
śuśubhe tanmahārāja kaṭakaṃ śubhakarmaṇaḥ .. 39 ..
śastreṇa saṃśodhayatāṃ bhuvaṃ bhūmipate nṛṇām ..
rājasākrāntavapuṣāmaprakāśaṃ vapurbabhau .. 1.205.40 ..
pārśvasthatoyasampūrṇadṛtayaśca tathā janāḥ ..
dhāvamānāḥ pradṛśyante vardhitā gṛhaśodhane .. 41 ..
abhyukṣayanti cāpyanye tṛṇaveśmāni pārthiva ..
taptānāṃ śītakāmānāṃ dṛtivaktrodgatairjalaiḥ .. 42 ..
abhiśrayeṇa dhūpena samantādākulīkṛtam ..
babhūva tasya kaṭakaṃ nīhāreṇaiva saṃyutam .. 43 ..
avaropitabhāṇḍānāṃ dāntānāṃ yadunandana ..
pṛṣṭhānyabhyukṣayāmāsurgomayena jalena ca .. 44 ..
kharoṣṭrasabalīvarda caraṇārthe vinirgatam .. 45 ..
1.177.d:
कृतानि क्रियमाणानि ददृशुस्तत्र मानवाः ॥
द्रुमैर्विश्राम्यमाणैश्च क्रियमाणैस्तथा कटैः ॥ 38 ॥
गृहैरारोप्यमाणैश्च पटोर्णातृणसंस्कृतैः ॥
शुशुभे तन्महाराज कटकं शुभकर्मणः ॥ 39 ॥
शस्त्रेण संशोधयतां भुवं भूमिपते नृणाम् ॥
राजसाक्रान्तवपुषामप्रकाशं वपुर्बभौ ॥ 1.205.40 ॥
पार्श्वस्थतोयसम्पूर्णदृतयश्च तथा जनाः ॥
धावमानाः प्रदृश्यन्ते वर्धिता गृहशोधने ॥ 41 ॥
अभ्युक्षयन्ति चाप्यन्ये तृणवेश्मानि पार्थिव ॥
तप्तानां शीतकामानां दृतिवक्त्रोद्गतैर्जलैः ॥ 42 ॥
अभिश्रयेण धूपेन समन्तादाकुलीकृतम् ॥
बभूव तस्य कटकं नीहारेणैव संयुतम् ॥ 43 ॥
अवरोपितभाण्डानां दान्तानां यदुनन्दन ॥
पृष्ठान्यभ्युक्षयामासुर्गोमयेन जलेन च ॥ 44 ॥
खरोष्ट्रसबलीवर्द चरणार्थे विनिर्गतम् ॥ 45 ॥
1.177.m:
men saw them made and being made. / With trees being cleared, with mats being prepared,
and with houses being erected, constructed of cloth, wool, and grass, / that camp of him of auspicious deeds shone, O great king.
As men were clearing the ground with weapons, O lord of the earth, / their bodies, covered with dust, shone indistinctly.
And people, with water-skins full of water at their sides, / were seen running about, employed in cleaning the houses.
And others sprinkled the grass huts, O king, / with water emerging from the mouths of leather bags, for those who were heated and desired coolness.
Confounded on all sides by incense on cooking stoves, / his camp became as if enveloped in mist.
For the tamed animals whose packs had been unloaded, O delight of the Yadus, / they sprinkled their backs with cow dung and water.
[A herd] of donkeys, camels, and oxen went forth for grazing.

1.177.s:
dadṛśe bahusāhasraṃ kaṭake bharatasya tu ..
rathebhyasturagānanye vimucya hayakovidāḥ .. 46 ..
avaropitabhāṇḍāni sāntvayāñcakrire śanaiḥ ..
samutthāya rajo bhaumaṃ turaṅgaparivartanaiḥ .. 47 ..
khamāruroha rājendra kapotāruṇapāṇḍuram ..
sthāpayāñcakrire cānye jalasthāne ca vājinaḥ .. 48 ..

vitānādhastathā kecitsthāpayāñcakrire hayān .. 49 ..
hayebhyo yavasaṃ dattvā kecidbubhujire janāḥ ..
kaṭacchāyāśca nāgānāṃ cakruścānye sahasraśaḥ ..1.205.50 ..
vitānāni ca mukhyāni sūryatāpapraśāntaye ..
snātāñjalāśaye nāgām̐llabdhatoyāñjanādhipa .. 51..
sacchannānsvaparīdhānakumbhānninyuḥ svamālayam ..
kaṭakāddūrataścakrurālānaṃ nṛpadantinām.. 52..
1.177.d:
ददृशे बहुसाहस्रं कटके भरतस्य तु ॥
रथेभ्यस्तुरगानन्ये विमुच्य हयकोविदाः ॥ 46 ॥
अवरोपितभाण्डानि सान्त्वयाञ्चक्रिरे शनैः ॥
समुत्थाय रजो भौमं तुरङ्गपरिवर्तनैः ॥ 47 ॥
खमारुरोह राजेन्द्र कपोतारुणपाण्डुरम् ॥
स्थापयाञ्चक्रिरे चान्ये जलस्थाने च वाजिनः ॥ 48 ॥
श्रेणी चक्रुस्तथैवान्ये कटच्छायासु पार्थिव ॥
वितानाधस्तथा केचित्स्थापयाञ्चक्रिरे हयान् ॥ 49 ॥
हयेभ्यो यवसं दत्त्वा केचिद्बुभुजिरे जनाः ॥
कटच्छायाश्च नागानां चक्रुश्चान्ये सहस्रशः ॥1.205.50 ॥
वितानानि च मुख्यानि सूर्यतापप्रशान्तये ॥
स्नाताञ्जलाशये नागाम्̐ल्लब्धतोयाञ्जनाधिप ॥ 51॥
सच्छन्नान्स्वपरीधानकुम्भान्निन्युः स्वमालयम् ॥
कटकाद्दूरतश्चक्रुरालानं नृपदन्तिनाम्॥ 52॥
1.177.m:
Many thousands [of them] were seen in the camp of Bharata. / But others, skilled with horses, unyoked the steeds from the chariots,
unloaded their gear, and gently soothed them. / Dust from the earth, rising up from the horses rolling over,
ascended to the sky, O best of kings, grayish-red and pale like a pigeon. / Others stationed the steeds at the watering place,
and others arranged them in rows in the shade of straw mats, O king. / Some stationed the horses under awnings.
Having given grass to the horses, some people ate. / Others made shades of straw mats by the thousands for the elephants,
and excellent awnings to relieve the heat of the sun. / The elephants bathed in the water reservoir, and having received water, O lord of men,
they brought them to their quarters, their frontal lobes covered with their own garments. / Far from the camp they set up tethering posts for the king's elephants.

1.177.s:
ālānāni mahārāja mahāvṛkṣeṣu mānavāḥ ..
ādāya gopinastatra kaṭakācca vidūrataḥ .. 53 ..
1.177.d:
आलानानि महाराज महावृक्षेषु मानवाः ॥
आदाय गोपिनस्तत्र कटकाच्च विदूरतः ॥ 53 ॥
1.177.m: Men [made] tethering posts on large trees, O great king. / Taking [their animals] far from the camp, the cowherds there

1.177.s:
gosaṅghānmahiṣīsaṅghāṃścakrurvyastānyathāsukham ..
kaṭake ca tathā ninyurgorasāni narādhipa .. 54 ..
1.177.d:
गोसङ्घान्महिषीसङ्घांश्चक्रुर्व्यस्तान्यथासुखम् ॥
कटके च तथा निन्युर्गोरसानि नराधिप ॥ 54 ॥
1.177.m: comfortably dispersed the herds of cows and herds of buffaloes. / And likewise, O lord of men, they brought milk products into the camp.

1.177.s:
kaṭakāpaṇyavīthīṃ ca sarvapaṇyavibhūṣitām ..
dadṛśuḥ puruṣāstatra ayodhyāmiva cāparām .. 55 ..
1.177.d:
कटकापण्यवीथीं च सर्वपण्यविभूषिताम् ॥
ददृशुः पुरुषास्तत्र अयोध्यामिव चापराम् ॥ 55 ॥
1.177.m: And the people there saw the market street of the camp, adorned with all wares, / as if it were a second Ayodhyā.

1.177.s:
sthānāni sarvavaidyānāṃsadhvajāni narādhipa..
sāgadāni ca dṛśyante kaṭake bharatasya tu..56..
1.177.d:
स्थानानि सर्ववैद्यानांसध्वजानि नराधिप॥
सागदानि च दृश्यन्ते कटके भरतस्य तु॥56॥
1.177.m: The stations of all the physicians, furnished with banners and with medicines, / were seen, O lord of men, in the camp of Bharata.

1.177.s:
senādhyakṣeṇa vīreṇa vijayena mahātmanā..
kṛtaṃ śāstrānusāreṇa skandhāvāraniveśanam .. 57 ..
1.177.d:
सेनाध्यक्षेण वीरेण विजयेन महात्मना॥
कृतं शास्त्रानुसारेण स्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् ॥ 57 ॥
1.177.m: By the heroic commander-in-chief, the great-souled Vijaya, / the layout of the encampment was executed according to the treatises.

1.177.s:
viveśa bharataḥ śrīmāṃścaturaṅgabalānvitaḥ ..
anvīyamāno vīrābhyāṃ putrābhyāṃ yadunandana .. 58 ..
1.177.d:
विवेश भरतः श्रीमांश्चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः ॥
अन्वीयमानो वीराभ्यां पुत्राभ्यां यदुनन्दन ॥ 58 ॥
1.177.m: The glorious Bharata, accompanied by the fourfold army, entered, / followed by his two heroic sons, O delight of the Yadus,

1.177.s:
puṣkareṇa ca vīreṇa takṣeṇa sumahātmanā ..
balamukhyaistathaivānyaiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ .. 59 ..
1.177.d:
पुष्करेण च वीरेण तक्षेण सुमहात्मना ॥
बलमुख्यैस्तथैवान्यैः सूतमागधबन्दिभिः ॥ 59 ॥
1.177.m: by the heroic Puṣkara and the very great-souled Takṣa, / as well as by other army commanders, and by bards, chroniclers, and heralds.

1.177.s:
śaṅkhavāditraśabdena paṭahānāṃ svanena ca ..
bharatasya gṛhadvāratoraṇāntikamāgatāḥ .. 1.205.60..
1.177.d:
शङ्खवादित्रशब्देन पटहानां स्वनेन च ॥
भरतस्य गृहद्वारतोरणान्तिकमागताः ॥ 1.205.60॥
1.177.m: With the sound of conch-shell instruments and the beat of kettle-drums, / they arrived near the gateway arch of Bharata's dwelling.

1.177.s:
babhūburbalamukhyāste dikṣu ye yadunandana ..
santyajya madhyamāṃ vīthīṃ praveśāya mahāmanāḥ .. 61 ..
1.177.d:
बभूबुर्बलमुख्यास्ते दिक्षु ये यदुनन्दन ॥
सन्त्यज्य मध्यमां वीथीं प्रवेशाय महामनाः ॥ 61 ॥
1.177.m: Those army commanders who were in the various quarters, O delight of the Yadus, / left the middle avenue for his entry, being magnanimous.

1.177.s:
bandibhiḥ khyāpyamānāṃstānnāmakarmāvadānataḥ ..
śiraḥkampena bharataḥ prairayatsvānniveśanān .. 62 ..
1.177.d:
बन्दिभिः ख्याप्यमानांस्तान्नामकर्मावदानतः ॥
शिरःकम्पेन भरतः प्रैरयत्स्वान्निवेशनान् ॥ 62 ॥
1.177.m: As they were being proclaimed by the heralds according to their names, deeds, and heroic exploits, / Bharata dismissed them to their own quarters with a nod of his head.

1.177.s:
balamukhyānviveśātha svagṛhaṃ sarvaṛddhimat ..
dviyojanādhvanā śrāntā bharatasya tu sainikāḥ .. 63 ..
1.177.d:
बलमुख्यान्विवेशाथ स्वगृहं सर्वऋद्धिमत् ॥
द्वियोजनाध्वना श्रान्ता भरतस्य तु सैनिकाः ॥ 63 ॥
1.177.m: [Dismissing] the army commanders, he then entered his own house, endowed with all prosperity. / The soldiers of Bharata, wearied by a journey of two yojanas,

1.177.s:
viviśurbhavanānsvānsvānbhejire śayanāni ca ..
praviśya veśmapravaraṃ bharato'pi yathāsukham ... .. 64 ..
1.177.d:
विविशुर्भवनान्स्वान्स्वान्भेजिरे शयनानि च ॥
प्रविश्य वेश्मप्रवरं भरतोऽपि यथासुखम् ॥॥। 64 ॥
1.177.m: entered their respective dwellings and resorted to their beds. / Having entered his excellent dwelling, Bharata, too, as he pleased,

1.177.s:
vijahāra mahārāja devarājasamadyutiḥ ..
krameṇānena dharmātmā bhūmipāla dinedine ..
āsasāda vrajanneva gaṅgāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm .. 65 ..
1.177.d:
विजहार महाराज देवराजसमद्युतिः ॥
क्रमेणानेन धर्मात्मा भूमिपाल दिनेदिने ॥
आससाद व्रजन्नेव गङ्गां त्रिपथगां नदीम् ॥ 65 ॥
1.177.m: diverted himself, O great king, equal in radiance to the king of the gods. / In this manner, day by day, the righteous ruler of the earth, / proceeding on his way, reached the river Gaṅgā that flows through the three worlds,

1.177.s:
surāṅganāpīnapayodharasthasaccandanakṣālanalabdhalakṣmīm ..
grīṣmārkatāpādvigalattuṣāravivṛddhaśītodapaṭottarīyām .. 66 ..
bharata-śailūṣākhyānopari ṭippaṇī
1.177.d:
सुराङ्गनापीनपयोधरस्थसच्चन्दनक्षालनलब्धलक्ष्मीम् ॥
ग्रीष्मार्कतापाद्विगलत्तुषारविवृद्धशीतोदपटोत्तरीयाम् ॥ 66 ॥
भरत-शैलूषाख्यानोपरि टिप्पणी
1.177.m:
which possessed beauty gained from washing away the pure sandalwood paste resting on the plump breasts of divine maidens, / and whose upper garment of cloth was the cool water increased by snow melting from the heat of the summer sun.
Note on the narrative of Bharata and Śailūṣa.

1.178.s:
1.206
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
niveśamakarodrājan gaṅgātīre sa rāghavaḥ ..
bharatasya tadā cakrurgaṅgāyāṃ jalamaṇḍapān .. 1 ..
1.178.d:
1.206
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
निवेशमकरोद्राजन् गङ्गातीरे स राघवः ॥
भरतस्य तदा चक्रुर्गङ्गायां जलमण्डपान् ॥ 1 ॥
1.178.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
That descendant of Raghu made his encampment on the bank of the Gaṅgā, O king. / Then they built water-pavilions in the Gaṅgā for Bharata,

1.178.s:
tathaiva balamukhyānāṃ prādhānyena narādhipa ..
sainikaśca janastasya prāpya tāṃ suranimnagām .. 2 ..
1.178.d:
तथैव बलमुख्यानां प्राधान्येन नराधिप ॥
सैनिकश्च जनस्तस्य प्राप्य तां सुरनिम्नगाम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.178.m: and likewise for the principal army commanders, O lord of men. / And his soldiering folk, having reached that river of the gods,

1.178.s:
sāphalyaṃ janmano mene tatyāja ca tathā klamam ..
sasnau papau payaḥ kāmaṃ harṣeṇa mahatā yutaḥ .. 3 ...
1.178.d:
साफल्यं जन्मनो मेने तत्याज च तथा क्लमम् ॥
सस्नौ पपौ पयः कामं हर्षेण महता युतः ॥ 3 ॥।
1.178.m: considered their birth fruitful and cast off their fatigue. / They bathed and drank water to their heart's content, filled with great joy.

1.178.s:
snāpayāñcakrire tatra turagāṃsturagapriyāḥ ..
kuñjarānsnāpayamāsurmahāmātrāstathaiva ca .. 4 ..
1.178.d:
स्नापयाञ्चक्रिरे तत्र तुरगांस्तुरगप्रियाः ॥
कुञ्जरान्स्नापयमासुर्महामात्रास्तथैव च ॥ 4 ॥
1.178.m: There, those fond of horses bathed their steeds, / and the mahouts likewise bathed their elephants.

1.178.s:
majjadbhirbahusāhasraiḥ kuñjarairjāhnavī nadī ..
kirātaviṣayaiḥ saiva virarāja yathopalaiḥ .. 5 ..
1.178.d:
मज्जद्भिर्बहुसाहस्रैः कुञ्जरैर्जाह्नवी नदी ॥
किरातविषयैः सैव विरराज यथोपलैः ॥ 5 ॥
1.178.m: With many thousands of plunging elephants, the river Jāhnavī / shone as if with boulders in the realm of the Kirātas.

1.178.s:
samutthitamahāmātrāndṛṣṭvābhyukṣaṇachadmanā ..
cikrīḍurdṛtibhiḥ kecidviviśurbāhubhistathā .. 6 ..
1.178.d:
समुत्थितमहामात्रान्दृष्ट्वाभ्युक्षणछद्मना ॥
चिक्रीडुर्दृतिभिः केचिद्विविशुर्बाहुभिस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥
1.178.m: Seeing the mahouts who had stood up, some played with leather water-bags / under the guise of sprinkling, and others entered [the river swimming] with their arms.

1.178.s:
gaṅgāmāsādya saṃhṛṣṭā bharatasya tu sainikāḥ ..
bharato'pi tathā snātaḥ kṛtadaivatapūjanaḥ ..7..
1.178.d:
गङ्गामासाद्य संहृष्टा भरतस्य तु सैनिकाः ॥
भरतोऽपि तथा स्नातः कृतदैवतपूजनः ॥7॥
1.178.m: Having reached the Gaṅgā, Bharata's soldiers were overjoyed. / Bharata too, having bathed and performed worship of the deities,

1.178.s:
śrāddhaṃ cakre mahātejā dadau dānaṃ tathaiva ca ..
dattvā tatra mahādānānājñāpayati yādava ..8..
1.178.d:
श्राद्धं चक्रे महातेजा ददौ दानं तथैव च ॥
दत्त्वा तत्र महादानानाज्ञापयति यादव ॥8॥
1.178.m: the greatly radiant one performed a śrāddha and likewise gave gifts. / Having given great gifts there, O descendant of Yadu, he commanded:

1.178.s:
śilpino mama kurvantu kūṭāgārānmanoramān ..
rātrau dīpaniveśārthaṃ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ..9..
1.178.d:
शिल्पिनो मम कुर्वन्तु कूटागारान्मनोरमान् ॥
रात्रौ दीपनिवेशार्थं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥9॥
1.178.m: 'Let my artisans construct charming floating pavilions / by hundreds and thousands, for the placement of lamps at night.

1.178.s:
ānīyantāṃ tathā nāvaḥ sainyasya taraṇāya me ..
kriyantāṃ carmanāvaśca plavāśca śataśastathā ..1.206.10..
1.178.d:
आनीयन्तां तथा नावः सैन्यस्य तरणाय मे ॥
क्रियन्तां चर्मनावश्च प्लवाश्च शतशस्तथा ॥1.206.10॥
1.178.m: Let boats also be brought for the crossing of my army, / and let leather boats and rafts be made by the hundreds.

1.178.s:
uttaraṃ pāramāsādya niveśaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā ..
paraṃ pāraṃ janā yāntu udayāstamayāntare ..11..
1.178.d:
उत्तरं पारमासाद्य निवेशः क्रियतां तथा ॥
परं पारं जना यान्तु उदयास्तमयान्तरे ॥11॥
1.178.m: Having reached the northern shore, let an encampment be made there as well. / Let the people go to the further shore between sunrise and sunset.'

1.178.s:
evamājñāya bharato vijahāra yathāsukham ..
prasāritakaro rājansarvatraiva divākaraḥ .. 12 ..
1.178.d:
एवमाज्ञाय भरतो विजहार यथासुखम् ॥
प्रसारितकरो राजन्सर्वत्रैव दिवाकरः ॥ 12 ॥
1.178.m: Having commanded thus, Bharata diverted himself as he pleased. / The sun, having stretched out its rays everywhere, O king,

1.178.s:
yayāvadarśanaṃ tatra bharatasyaiva lajjayā ..
padmapatradalāgrābhā pratīcī cābhavatkṣaṇāt ..13..
1.178.d:
ययावदर्शनं तत्र भरतस्यैव लज्जया ॥
पद्मपत्रदलाग्राभा प्रतीची चाभवत्क्षणात् ॥13॥
1.178.m: went out of sight there, as if out of bashfulness before Bharata; / and the western quarter instantly became radiant like the tip of a lotus petal.

1.178.s:
ādityestamanuprāpte sandhyārāgānurañjitā ..
tatastu tamasā vyāpte na prājñāyata kiñcana .. 14 ..
1.178.d:
आदित्येस्तमनुप्राप्ते सन्ध्यारागानुरञ्जिता ॥
ततस्तु तमसा व्याप्ते न प्राज्ञायत किञ्चन ॥ 14 ॥
1.178.m: When the sun reached its setting, [the west] was tinted with the glow of twilight. / Then, when it was pervaded by darkness, nothing could be discerned.

1.178.s:
bharatājñākṛtānpūrvaṃ kūṭāgārānsadīpakān ..
dhvajamālāparikṣiptāṃścikṣipurjāhnavījale ..15..
1.178.d:
भरताज्ञाकृतान्पूर्वं कूटागारान्सदीपकान् ॥
ध्वजमालापरिक्षिप्तांश्चिक्षिपुर्जाह्नवीजले ॥15॥
1.178.m: They cast into the water of the Jāhnavī the floating pavilions equipped with lamps / and surrounded by garlands of banners, which had previously been made at Bharata's command.

1.178.s:
sainikaiśca tathā mukhyairbharatasya pṛthakpṛthak .
gaṅgāmbhasi parikṣiptā dīpavṛkṣāḥ sahasraśaḥ ..16..
1.178.d:
सैनिकैश्च तथा मुख्यैर्भरतस्य पृथक्पृथक् ।
गङ्गाम्भसि परिक्षिप्ता दीपवृक्षाः सहस्रशः ॥16॥
1.178.m: And likewise, by the chief soldiers of Bharata, individually, / lamp-trees were cast into the water of the Gaṅgā by the thousands.

1.178.s:
sā dīpamālinī gaṅgā tīradyotitavigrahī ..
jahāsa phenahāsena jihveva gaganapriyā .. 17 ..
1.178.d:
सा दीपमालिनी गङ्गा तीरद्योतितविग्रही ॥
जहास फेनहासेन जिह्वेव गगनप्रिया ॥ 17 ॥
1.178.m: Garlanded with lamps, her body illuminated along the bank, / the Gaṅgā laughed with the laughter of foam, like a tongue beloved of the sky.

1.178.s:
jalāntarāgatai rdīpairdīpavṛkṣairmanoharaiḥ ..
tathā kallolasaṃkrāntairgaṅgā dīpteva lakṣyate .. 18 ..
1.178.d:
जलान्तरागतै र्दीपैर्दीपवृक्षैर्मनोहरैः ॥
तथा कल्लोलसंक्रान्तैर्गङ्गा दीप्तेव लक्ष्यते ॥ 18 ॥
1.178.m: With the lamps that had moved into the water, with the delightful lamp-trees, / and with [reflections] transferred onto the billows, the Gaṅgā appeared as if ablaze.

1.178.s:
evaṃ hi krīḍatāṃ tatra gaṅgātīre tathā nṛṇām ..
rātrāvevāñjasā jagmurnāvo bahuvidhā nṛpa .. 19 ..
1.178.d:
एवं हि क्रीडतां तत्र गङ्गातीरे तथा नृणाम् ॥
रात्रावेवाञ्जसा जग्मुर्नावो बहुविधा नृप ॥ 19 ॥
1.178.m: While the men were thus sporting on the bank of the Gaṅgā, / various kinds of boats went swiftly across that very night, O king.

1.178.s:
śaśāṅkarājahaṃsena dṛṣṭvā khasarasīṃ janāḥ ..
ākramyamāṇā suṣupurniśīthe nidrayānvitāḥ .. 1.206.20 ..
1.178.d:
शशाङ्कराजहंसेन दृष्ट्वा खसरसीं जनाः ॥
आक्रम्यमाणा सुषुपुर्निशीथे निद्रयान्विताः ॥ 1.206.20 ॥
1.178.m: Having seen the lake of the sky [lit] by the royal swan of the hare-marked [moon], / the people, overcome at midnight, fell asleep, seized by slumber.

1.178.s:
śaśāṅkodayasaṃsuptabalaṃ padmavanopamam ..
nibodhayāmāsa tathā divākarakarotkaram .. 21 ..
1.178.d:
शशाङ्कोदयसंसुप्तबलं पद्मवनोपमम् ॥
निबोधयामास तथा दिवाकरकरोत्करम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.178.m: The mass of sunbeams awakened the army, / which was like a lotus thicket sleeping at moonrise.

1.178.s:
cakṛṣuste tadā nāvaḥ karṇadhārā yathā svakāḥ ..
balaṃ ca sakalaṃ pāraṃ tārayā ñcakrire tadā .. 22 ..
1.178.d:
चकृषुस्ते तदा नावः कर्णधारा यथा स्वकाः ॥
बलं च सकलं पारं तारया ञ्चक्रिरे तदा ॥ 22 ॥
1.178.m: Then the helmsmen pulled their boats, / and they carried the entire army across to the other shore.

1.178.s:
nāvastāṃ kiṅkiṇījālaiḥ patākābhiśca rājitā ..
ninyurbalaṃ paraṃ pāraṃ karṇadhārasphigāhatāḥ .. 23 ..
1.178.d:
नावस्तां किङ्किणीजालैः पताकाभिश्च राजिता ॥
निन्युर्बलं परं पारं कर्णधारस्फिगाहताः ॥ 23 ॥
1.178.m: Those boats, adorned with nets of small bells and flags, / struck by the helmsmen's oars, transported the army to the farther bank.

1.178.s:
bhāṇḍaiḥ pūrṇāstathā kāścitkāścitpūrṇā janena ca ..
turaṅgamaistathā pūrṇā gokharoṣṭraistathā parāḥ .. 24 ..
1.178.d:
भाण्डैः पूर्णास्तथा काश्चित्काश्चित्पूर्णा जनेन च ॥
तुरङ्गमैस्तथा पूर्णा गोखरोष्ट्रैस्तथा पराः ॥ 24 ॥
1.178.m: Some were filled with baggage, and some with people; / others were filled with horses, and others with cattle, donkeys, and camels.

1.178.s:
kāścitsakuñjarā nāvo yayuḥ pāraṃ tadā param ..
tathā padmadalākṣīṇāṃ strīṇāṃ nāvaśca pūritāḥ .. 25 ..
1.178.d:
काश्चित्सकुञ्जरा नावो ययुः पारं तदा परम् ॥
तथा पद्मदलाक्षीणां स्त्रीणां नावश्च पूरिताः ॥ 25 ॥
1.178.m: Some boats, carrying elephants, went to the farther shore; / and boats were filled with lotus-petal-eyed women.

1.178.s:
vimānābhāḥ pradṛśyante gaṅgāmbhasi nareśvara ..
karṇadhāravaropetā daṇḍibhiḥ puruṣairvṛtāḥ .. 26 ..
1.178.d:
विमानाभाः प्रदृश्यन्ते गङ्गाम्भसि नरेश्वर ॥
कर्णधारवरोपेता दण्डिभिः पुरुषैर्वृताः ॥ 26 ॥
1.178.m: Looking like celestial chariots on the water of the Gaṅgā, O king, / they were equipped with excellent helmsmen and attended by men with poles.

1.178.s:
lokasantāraṇārthāya bhūyo jagmustathā parāḥ ..
carmanaubhistathā kecitplavaiḥ kecitsuyantritaiḥ .. 27 ..
1.178.d:
लोकसन्तारणार्थाय भूयो जग्मुस्तथा पराः ॥
चर्मनौभिस्तथा केचित्प्लवैः केचित्सुयन्त्रितैः ॥ 27 ॥
1.178.m: Others went across again to transport the folk; / some [crossed] on skin-boats, and some on well-rigged rafts.

1.178.s:
jagmurādāya bhāṇḍāni dṛtibhiśca tathā kvacit ..
narairdṛtisamārūḍhaiḥ kṛṣyamāṇāsturaṅgamāḥ .. 28 ..
1.178.d:
जग्मुरादाय भाण्डानि दृतिभिश्च तथा क्वचित् ॥
नरैर्दृतिसमारूढैः कृष्यमाणास्तुरङ्गमाः ॥ 28 ॥
1.178.m: Taking the baggage, they went across on inflated skins in places; / horses, pulled by men mounted on inflated skins,

1.178.s:
jagmuḥ kecitparaṃ pāraṃ bāhubhirmanujeśvara ..
jagmuranye paraṃ pāraṃ saṃgṛhītāśca raśmibhiḥ .. .. 29 ..
1.178.d:
जग्मुः केचित्परं पारं बाहुभिर्मनुजेश्वर ॥
जग्मुरन्ये परं पारं संगृहीताश्च रश्मिभिः ॥ ॥ 29 ॥
1.178.m: swam to the other shore with their limbs, O lord of men; / others went to the other shore held by their reins.

1.178.s:
nausthaireva paraiḥ śīghraṃ turagā nṛpabāhubhiḥ ..
mahiṣīṇāṃ ca saṅghāni gavāṃ ca yadunandana .. 1.206.30 ..
1.178.d:
नौस्थैरेव परैः शीघ्रं तुरगा नृपबाहुभिः ॥
महिषीणां च सङ्घानि गवां च यदुनन्दन ॥ 1.206.30 ॥
1.178.m: Swiftly [steered] by their arms by other men standing in boats, O king, were the horses; / and herds of she-buffaloes and cattle, O joy of the Yadus,

1.178.s:
jagmurgopālakaiḥ sārdhaṃ paraṃ pāraṃ ca bāhubhiḥ ..
uṣṭragardabhasaṃghāni tāryamāṇāni bāhubhiḥ .. 31 ..
1.178.d:
जग्मुर्गोपालकैः सार्धं परं पारं च बाहुभिः ॥
उष्ट्रगर्दभसंघानि तार्यमाणानि बाहुभिः ॥ 31 ॥
1.178.m: went with the cowherds to the farther shore by their arms [swimming]; / herds of camels and donkeys being made to cross by force of arms,

1.178.s:
bhūyobhūyo nyavartanta tatra rāvo mahānabhūt ..
tīrṇasya tāryamāṇasya narasya yadusattama .. 32 ..
1.178.d:
भूयोभूयो न्यवर्तन्त तत्र रावो महानभूत् ॥
तीर्णस्य तार्यमाणस्य नरस्य यदुसत्तम ॥ 32 ॥
1.178.m: turned back again and again, and a great clamour arose there; / of a man who had crossed over and of one being carried across, O best of the Yadus,

1.178.s:
āsītkolāhalo ghorastīrayorubhayorapi ..
bharato'pi mahātejāḥ snāto hutahutāśanaḥ .. 33 ..
1.178.d:
आसीत्कोलाहलो घोरस्तीरयोरुभयोरपि ॥
भरतोऽपि महातेजाः स्नातो हुतहुताशनः ॥ 33 ॥

1.178.m:
King Bharata, whose might was equal to Śakra, having crossed that goddess / who rests on the crags of Mahādeva’s matted locks and whose cool waters are enhanced by contact with the moon, / brought [the crossing] to completion.
1.207 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When Bharata had crossed the Gaṅgā, the sky’s girdle, / another Kaurava king entered his camp, O king,
accompanied by a fourfold army resembling an ocean, / and the ruler of the Kirātas, the king named Damana.
He appeared with forces comprising many thousands of scent-elephants; / having honoured him appropriately, Bharata, who loved dharma,
reached the Yamunā, the daughter of the sun who destroys sins, / the holy sister of Yama, a lovely dark garland.
Indeed, having performed a śrāddha anywhere in that river, O lord of men, / one obtains imperishable reward and rejoices in the heights of heaven.
Bathed [in it] on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight and having worshipped the daughter of the sun, / one is freed from all sins and goes to the heavenly realm.

1.178.m:
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, before sunrise, / he who has bathed in it and worshipped Dharmarāja with water and sesame seeds
does not fall into a bad rebirth and redeems his family; / indeed, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, in whatever river
he has bathed, in all river waters, he is freed from sins; / but in the Yamunā especially, because she is the sister of Yama.
Having bathed in the Yamunā's water and gratified the ancestors and gods, / he does not go to a bad rebirth and goes to the realm of heaven.
Having reached that Yamunā, just as [he had done with] the water of the Gaṅgā, / sporting thus, Bharata crossed the great river.
When the great-souled Bharata had crossed the Yamunā, / Suratha, king of the Matsyas, then entered his camp,
and Gorasena of the Sālvas, and Prabhadraka of the Śibis; / with those rulers of men, he approached Kurukṣetra,
concerning which this ancient verse circulates in the world: / “Even the dust of Kurukṣetra stirred up by the wind

all reach heaven and shine in the sky like gods; / where, O best of kings, is the sacred place Sannīti, famous throughout the three worlds.
It is celebrated as Sannīti precisely because of bringing together the holy places; / all the holy places and lakes on earth down to the ocean
always come there constantly at the end of the month, O Yādava; / and whoever performs a śrāddha there when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu
obtains the foremost fruit of a hundred horse sacrifices. / Having reached there, Bharata then dwelt happily,
and asked the brahmins there the cause of the holy place Sannīti; / then, being questioned by Bharata, the brahmin Ghaṭodara
spoke to Bharata a tale that destroys sins. / Ghaṭodara said: / When Śakra was overcome with the killing of Vṛtra and the three worlds fell into the power of the Daityas,

सब्रह्मकाः सुराः सर्वे विष्णुं शरणमाययुः ॥
तानुवाच हरिर्देवश्च्यवनस्यात्मसम्भवः ॥ 22 ॥
भार्गवो ब्राह्मणः श्रीमान्दधीच इति विश्रुतः ॥
अस्थिभिः क्रियतां तस्य देवेन्द्रस्य वरायुधम् ॥ 23 ॥
प्रविश्य देवांस्तत्राहं हन्ता वृत्रमसंशयम् ॥
एवमुक्ताः सुराः सर्वे दधीचस्याश्रमं ययुः ॥ 24 ॥
ददृशुश्च महाभागं दधीचं तपसां निधिम् ॥
पूजयित्वा महाभागं तमूचुः संहताः सुरा॥। 25 ॥
त्वदस्थिभिः करिष्यामो वज्रं दैत्यनिबर्हणम् ॥
अन्यानि च तथास्त्राणि सुरकार्यार्थसिद्धये ॥ 26 ॥
तत्र त्वं देवकार्यार्थं संन्यासं द्विज रोचय ॥
एवमुक्तो दधीचस्तु प्रत्युवाच स तान्सुरान् ॥ 27 ॥
तीर्थयात्रा प्रतिज्ञाता सर्वतीर्थेषु वै मया ॥
तां तु कृत्वा करिष्यामि देहन्यासं सुरोत्तमाः ॥ 28 ॥
1.178.m:
all the gods along with Brahmā went to Viṣṇu for refuge; / the divine lord Hari, Cyavana's manifestation, said to them:
"There is a glorious Bhārgava brahmin renowned as Dadhīca. / Let an excellent weapon be made for the lord of the gods from his bones.
Entering [the weapon] there, O gods, I will slay Vṛtra beyond doubt." / Addressed in this way, all the gods went to the hermitage of Dadhīca.
They saw the illustrious Dadhīca, a treasury of austerities. / Having worshipped that illustrious one, the assembled gods said to him:
"With your bones we will make the vajra that destroys the daityas, / as well as other divine weapons for the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods.
Therefore, O twice-born, consent to renunciation for the purpose of the gods." / Addressed in this way, Dadhīca replied to those gods:
"A pilgrimage has been vowed by me to all sacred bathing places. / Having made that [pilgrimage], O best of gods, I will lay down my body."
