दधीच उवाच ॥
अद्य प्रभृति मासान्ते भवद्भिः सततं सुराः ॥ 33 ॥
सान्निध्यमिह कर्तव्यं तीर्थैश्चैव यथागतैः ॥
घटोदर उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तैस्तथेत्युक्तो देवैस्तीर्थैश्च स त्वथ ॥ 34 ॥
त्यक्त्वा देहं दिवं यातो दधीचः स्वेन तेजसा ॥
विश्वकर्मा च तस्यास्थ्नां भागैर्वज्रमथा करोत् ॥ 35 ॥
1.178.m:
The gods said: / "You are capable of summoning all the sacred bathing places, O bull among the twice-born. / May all the sacred bathing places come here this very day for you, O sinless one,
by your splendor, O Bhārgava, and likewise by ours." / Ghaṭodara said: / Addressed in this way by all the gods, the sacred bathing places, as well as the rivers,
the lakes, and the oceans came there, O ruler of men, / through their great affection, O king, and through his supreme yoga.
And perceiving their presence, the best of the twice-born bathed there; / and having performed the water-offering to the gods along with the ancestors,
he spoke these meaningful words to the gods standing there: / Dadhīca said: / "From this day forward, at the end of each month, O gods, continuously,
presence must be maintained here by you and by the sacred bathing places as they have arrived." / Ghaṭodara said: / When addressed in this way, having been answered, "So be it," by the gods and by the sacred bathing places, he then,
having abandoned his body, Dadhīca went to heaven through his own splendor. / And Viśvakarman then fashioned the vajra from portions of his bones,

1.178.s:
āyudhāni ca devānāṃ tathaiva ca pṛthakpṛthak ..
tena vajreṇa mahatā vṛtraṃ hatvā mahāsuram .. 36 ..
jaghāna daityamukhyānāṃ navatirnavatistathā ..
tataḥ prabhṛti māsānte nityameva raghūdvaha .. 37 ..
sānnidhyamiha tīrthānāṃ devatānāṃ ca kalpitam ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
etacchrutvā mahātejā dattvā dānāni rāghavaḥ .. 38 ..
yayau sainyena mahatā bharato'marakaṇṭakam ..
tatra viṣṇupadaṃ prāpya pūjayitvā ca rāghavaḥ ..39..
1.178.d:
आयुधानि च देवानां तथैव च पृथक्पृथक् ॥
तेन वज्रेण महता वृत्रं हत्वा महासुरम् ॥ 36 ॥
जघान दैत्यमुख्यानां नवतिर्नवतिस्तथा ॥
ततः प्रभृति मासान्ते नित्यमेव रघूद्वह ॥ 37 ॥
सान्निध्यमिह तीर्थानां देवतानां च कल्पितम् ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा महातेजा दत्त्वा दानानि राघवः ॥ 38 ॥
ययौ सैन्येन महता भरतोऽमरकण्टकम् ॥
तत्र विष्णुपदं प्राप्य पूजयित्वा च राघवः ॥39॥
1.178.m:
and likewise weapons for the gods, each separately. / Having slain the great asura Vṛtra with that great vajra,
he also killed ninety times ninety chief daityas. / From then on, at the end of each month, always, O scion of Raghu,
the presence of the sacred bathing places and the deities was established here. / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having heard this, the mighty Bharata, giving gifts,
went with a great army to Amarakaṇṭaka. / Reaching the Viṣṇupada there and worshipping, the scion of Raghu

1.178.s:
āsasāda nadīṃ gaurīṃ puṇyāṃ pāpabhayāpahām ..
viśvāmitrājñayā rakṣaḥ praviveśa purā nṛpam .. 1.207.40 ..
1.178.d:
आससाद नदीं गौरीं पुण्यां पापभयापहाम् ॥
विश्वामित्राज्ञया रक्षः प्रविवेश पुरा नृपम् ॥ 1.207.40 ॥
1.178.m: reached the holy river Gaurī, which removes fear of sin. / Formerly, by the command of Viśvāmitra, a rakṣas entered King [Saudāsa],

1.178.s:
kaśāhatena mārgasthaṃ śaptaṃ bhūpāla śaktinā ..
saudāsaṃ sa praviṣṭastu bhakṣayāmāsa śaktinam .. 41 ..
1.178.d:
कशाहतेन मार्गस्थं शप्तं भूपाल शक्तिना ॥
सौदासं स प्रविष्टस्तु भक्षयामास शक्तिनम् ॥ 41 ॥
1.178.m: who had been cursed, O king, by Śakti standing in the path whom he struck with a whip. / Having entered Saudāsa, it devoured Śakti;

1.178.s:
tataḥ putraśataṃ rājanvasiṣṭhasyaiva satvaraḥ ..
hṛte putraśate dukhādvasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ .. 42 ..
1.178.d:
ततः पुत्रशतं राजन्वसिष्ठस्यैव सत्वरः ॥
हृते पुत्रशते दुखाद्वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ॥ 42 ॥
1.178.m: then quickly [it devoured] the hundred sons of Vasiṣṭha himself, O king. / When his hundred sons were carried off, out of sorrow the blessed sage Vasiṣṭha

1.178.s:
viveśa nimnagāṃ gaurīṃ prāṇatyāgacikīrṣayā ..
viprasya bhūpa yātasya vidrutā sā tadābhavat .. 43 ..
1.178.d:
विवेश निम्नगां गौरीं प्राणत्यागचिकीर्षया ॥
विप्रस्य भूप यातस्य विद्रुता सा तदाभवत् ॥ 43 ॥
1.178.m: entered the river Gaurī, wishing to abandon his life. / When the brahmin went into it, O king, she then fled in all directions.

1.178.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti loke'smiñchatadruriti śabditā .. śatadru
sarvapāpapraśamanī sarvakalyāṇakāriṇī..44..
1.178.d:
ततः प्रभृति लोकेऽस्मिञ्छतद्रुरिति शब्दिता ॥ शतद्रु
सर्वपापप्रशमनी सर्वकल्याणकारिणी॥44॥
1.178.m: From then on in this world she was called Śatadru, / calming all sins, bringing all auspiciousness,

1.178.s:
snātānāṃ ca tathā rājandaśadhenuphalapradā ..
tāṃ samāsādya tatrāpi dattvā dānaṃ sa rāghavaḥ..45..
1.178.d:
स्नातानां च तथा राजन्दशधेनुफलप्रदा ॥
तां समासाद्य तत्रापि दत्त्वा दानं स राघवः॥45॥
1.178.m: and granting the fruit of ten cows to those who bathe [in her], O king. / Reaching her, the scion of Raghu gave gifts there too,

1.178.s:
uttīrya tāṃ yayau tatra sā cāntyā yatra nimnagā ..
yasyāṃ snātvā vimucyante sarvapāpabhayairnarāḥ ..46..
1.178.d:
उत्तीर्य तां ययौ तत्र सा चान्त्या यत्र निम्नगा ॥
यस्यां स्नात्वा विमुच्यन्ते सर्वपापभयैर्नराः ॥46॥
1.178.m: and having crossed her, he went where the river Antyā was, / bathing in which men are freed from all fears of sin,

1.178.s:
yasyāṃ snānādavāpnoti daśagodānajaṃ phalam ..
āṣāḍhe ca tathā kṛtvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet .. 47 ..
1.178.d:
यस्यां स्नानादवाप्नोति दशगोदानजं फलम् ॥
आषाढे च तथा कृत्वा गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥ 47 ॥
1.178.m: and by bathing in which one obtains the fruit born of gifting ten cows; / and having done so in [the month of] Āṣāḍha, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.

1.178.s:
gaurītoyādvinirmukto vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ ..
pāśabandhabharairyasyāṃ papāta sahasā nṛpa ..48..
1.178.d:
गौरीतोयाद्विनिर्मुक्तो वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ॥
पाशबन्धभरैर्यस्यां पपात सहसा नृप ॥48॥
1.178.m: Released from the waters of the Gaurī, the blessed sage Vasiṣṭha, / laden with bonds of fetters, fell suddenly into her, O king;

1.178.s:
vipāśaśca tathā devyā kṛtvā tīre visarjitaḥ .. vipāśā
śaktiputraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā vasiṣṭho'pi parāśaram .. 49 ..
1.178.d:
विपाशश्च तथा देव्या कृत्वा तीरे विसर्जितः ॥ विपाशा
शक्तिपुत्रं ततो दृष्ट्वा वसिष्ठोऽपि पराशरम् ॥ 49 ॥
1.178.m: and made free from fetters (vipāśa) by the goddess, he was cast out onto the bank. / Then, seeing Parāśara, the son of Śakti,

1.178.s:
asti santānamityuktvā maraṇādvinivartata ..
sā cāntyā ca tathā loke vipāśetyabhidhīyate .. 1.207.50 ..
1.178.d:
अस्ति सन्तानमित्युक्त्वा मरणाद्विनिवर्तत ॥
सा चान्त्या च तथा लोके विपाशेत्यभिधीयते ॥ 1.207.50 ॥
1.178.m: and saying, "There is offspring," Vasiṣṭha turned back from death. / And in the world that river Antyā is named Vipāśā.

1.178.s:
vipāśāṃ ca samuttīrṇe bharate dharmavatsale ..
viveśa kaṭakaṃ tasya kuṇideśo mahodayaḥ .. 51 ..
1.178.d:
विपाशां च समुत्तीर्णे भरते धर्मवत्सले ॥
विवेश कटकं तस्य कुणिदेशो महोदयः ॥ 51 ॥
1.178.m: When Bharata, fond of dharma, had crossed the Vipāśā, / the ruler of the Kuṇi land, the illustrious one, entered his camp,

1.178.s:
traigarto vasudhānaśca kulūtādhipatirjayaḥ ..
dāśerakastathā rājā govāśana iti śrutaḥ .. 52 ..
1.178.d:
त्रैगर्तो वसुधानश्च कुलूताधिपतिर्जयः ॥
दाशेरकस्तथा राजा गोवाशन इति श्रुतः ॥ 52 ॥
1.178.m: along with the king of Trigarta, Vasudhāna, and Jaya, the lord of Kulūta, / and the king of the Dāśerakas known as Govāśana.

1.178.s:
irāvatīṃ śīghragamāṃ bharato'pi tadā yayau ..
daśadhenuphalaṃ yatra snāta eva samaśnute .. 53 ..
1.178.d:
इरावतीं शीघ्रगमां भरतोऽपि तदा ययौ ॥
दशधेनुफलं यत्र स्नात एव समश्नुते ॥ 53 ॥
1.178.m: Bharata then went to the swift-flowing Irāvatī, / where merely by bathing one enjoys the fruit of ten cows.

1.178.s:
ṣaṣṭitīrthasahasrāṇi vahatyekā irāvatī ..
aṣṭamyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa yatra yujyeta revatī .. 54 ..
1.178.d:
षष्टितीर्थसहस्राणि वहत्येका इरावती ॥
अष्टम्यां तु विशेषेण यत्र युज्येत रेवती ॥ 54 ॥
1.178.m: The single Irāvatī carries sixty thousand sacred bathing places, / especially on the eighth day when Revatī is joined [with it].

1.178.s:
tatra dattvā bahuvidhaṃ dānaṃ raghukulodvahaḥ ..
uttīrya tāṃ yayau śīghraṃ devikāṃ pāpanāśinīm .. 59 ..
1.178.d:
तत्र दत्त्वा बहुविधं दानं रघुकुलोद्वहः ॥
उत्तीर्य तां ययौ शीघ्रं देविकां पापनाशिनीम् ॥ 59 ॥
1.178.m: Having given various gifts there, the scion of the lineage of Raghu, / having crossed her, went swiftly to the sin-destroying Devikā,

1.178.s:
dṛṣṭamātraiva yā devī sarvakalmaṣanāśinī ..
śarīrabahulā sā tu harasya dayitā umā .. 56 ..
1.178.d:
दृष्टमात्रैव या देवी सर्वकल्मषनाशिनी ॥
शरीरबहुला सा तु हरस्य दयिता उमा ॥ 56 ॥
1.178.m: which goddess destroys all defilements as soon as she is seen; / she, having many bodies, is Umā, the beloved of Hara.

1.178.s:
tatrāpi dattvā dānāni pūjayāmāsa śaṅkaram ..
bharate cātha tatrasthe viviśuḥ pañca pārthivāḥ .. 57 ..
1.178.d:
तत्रापि दत्त्वा दानानि पूजयामास शङ्करम् ॥
भरते चाथ तत्रस्थे विविशुः पञ्च पार्थिवाः ॥ 57 ॥
1.178.m: Having given gifts there too, he worshipped Śaṅkara. / And while Bharata was staying there, five mountain kings

1.178.s:
pārvatīyā mahārāja padātigaṇasaṅkulāḥ ..
kumāraḥ śreṇimāñchūro balabandhuḥ suyodhanaḥ .. 58 ..
1.178.d:
पार्वतीया महाराज पदातिगणसङ्कुलाः ॥
कुमारः श्रेणिमाञ्छूरो बलबन्धुः सुयोधनः ॥ 58 ॥
1.178.m: crowded with multitudes of foot-soldiers entered [his camp], O great king: / Kumāra, Śreṇimat, the heroic Balabandhu, Suyodhana,

1.178.s:
madrarājoṃ'śumāṃścaiva tathaiva ca mahābalaḥ ..
pūjito madrarājena śākalena narottamaḥ .. 59 ..
1.178.d:
मद्रराजोंऽशुमांश्चैव तथैव च महाबलः ॥
पूजितो मद्रराजेन शाकलेन नरोत्तमः ॥ 59 ॥
1.178.m: and the mighty king of Madra, Aṃśumat. / Worshipped by the king of Madra, the ruler of Śākala, that best of men,

1.178.s:
trirātramuṣitaḥ śrīmāṃścandrabhāgāṃ nadīṃ yayau ..
candrāṃśuśītalajalāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm .. 1.207.60 ..
1.178.d:
त्रिरात्रमुषितः श्रीमांश्चन्द्रभागां नदीं ययौ ॥
चन्द्रांशुशीतलजलां सर्वपापप्रणाशिनीम् ॥ 1.207.60 ॥
1.178.m: the glorious one, having dwelt three nights, went to the river Candrabhāgā, / whose waters are cool like moonbeams, which destroys all sins,

1.178.s:
bahutīrthasamāyuktāṃ snānātsarvapradāṃ nṛṇām .. .
viśeṣeṇa mahārāja māghapuṣyatrayodaśīm .. 61 ..
1.178.d:
बहुतीर्थसमायुक्तां स्नानात्सर्वप्रदां नृणाम् ॥ ।
विशेषेण महाराज माघपुष्यत्रयोदशीम् ॥ 61 ॥
1.178.m: endowed with many sacred bathing places, granting everything to men through bathing, / especially on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight in Māgha with Puṣya, O great king.

1.178.s:
bharate tāṃ samuttīrṇe viveśa kaṭakaṃ tataḥ ..
etacchrutañjayaḥ śrīmānabhicāraḥ kṛtañjayaḥ .. 62 .. .
1.178.d:
भरते तां समुत्तीर्णे विवेश कटकं ततः ॥
एतच्छ्रुतञ्जयः श्रीमानभिचारः कृतञ्जयः ॥ 62 ॥ ।
1.178.m: When Bharata had crossed her, there entered his camp / the glorious Śrutañjaya, Abhicāra, Kṛtañjaya,

1.178.s:
kāśmīrakaśca dharmātmā subāhuriti viśrutaḥ ..
āsasāda sa taiḥ sārddhaṃ vitastāṃ tu mahānadīm ..63..
1.178.d:
काश्मीरकश्च धर्मात्मा सुबाहुरिति विश्रुतः ॥
आससाद स तैः सार्द्धं वितस्तां तु महानदीम् ॥63॥
1.178.m: and the righteous ruler of Kashmir known as Subāhu. / Together with them, he reached the great river Vitastā,

1.178.s:
svargalokapradāṃ snāne sarvakalmaṣanāśinīm ..
proṣṭhapādasya māsasya śuklapakṣatrayodaśīm .. 64 ..
1.178.d:
स्वर्गलोकप्रदां स्नाने सर्वकल्मषनाशिनीम् ॥
प्रोष्ठपादस्य मासस्य शुक्लपक्षत्रयोदशीम् ॥ 64 ॥
1.178.m: which grants the heavenly world upon bathing, destroys all defilements, / [and is] especially holy and supremely purifying

1.178.s:
viśeṣeṇa mahārāja puṇyāṃ paramapāvanīm ..
bharatastāṃ samuttīrya sudāmāṃ caiva nimnagām .. 65 ..
1.178.d:
विशेषेण महाराज पुण्यां परमपावनीम् ॥
भरतस्तां समुत्तीर्य सुदामां चैव निम्नगाम् ॥ 65 ॥
1.178.m: on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Proṣṭhapada, O great king. / Bharata, having crossed her and also the river Sudāmā,

1.178.s:
āsasāda mahātejāḥ kaikeyānyadunandana ..
balena caturaṅgeṇa yudhājitkaikayādhipaḥ .. 66 ..
1.178.d:
आससाद महातेजाः कैकेयान्यदुनन्दन ॥
बलेन चतुरङ्गेण युधाजित्कैकयाधिपः ॥ 66 ॥
1.178.m: the mighty one reached the lands of the Kaikeyas, O delight of the Yadus. / With a fourfold army, Yudhājit, the king of the Kaikayas,

1.178.s:
niryayau bharataṃ prāptaṃ śrutvā bharatamātulaḥ ..
nāgarāśca tathā mukhyā rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ .. 67 ..
1.178.d:
निर्ययौ भरतं प्राप्तं श्रुत्वा भरतमातुलः ॥
नागराश्च तथा मुख्या राजगृहनिवासिनः ॥ 67 ॥
1.178.m: Hearing that Bharata had arrived, Bharata's maternal uncle came forth, / as did the leading citizens residing in Rājagṛha.

1.178.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyā ye ca varṇavarā janāḥ ..
yānairuccāvacaiḥ sarvai nagarāttu vinirgatāḥ .. 68 ..
1.178.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्त्रिया वैश्या ये च वर्णवरा जनाः ॥
यानैरुच्चावचैः सर्वै नगरात्तु विनिर्गताः ॥ 68 ॥
1.178.m: Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and people who were the best of the castes, / went forth from the city in all kinds of high and low vehicles.

1.178.s:
vāditrānpurataḥ kṛtvā gaṇikāśca vinirgatāḥ ..
pratigrahanimittaṃ tu rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ .. 69 ..
1.178.d:
वादित्रान्पुरतः कृत्वा गणिकाश्च विनिर्गताः ॥
प्रतिग्रहनिमित्तं तु राघवस्य महात्मनः ॥ 69 ॥
1.178.m: Courtesans also went forth, placing musical instruments in front, / for the sake of welcoming the high-souled descendant of Raghu.

1.178.s:
bharato'pi mahātejāḥ sa sametya yudhājitā ..
abhyadhāvata tatprītyā mātulaṃ kaikayādhipam ..1.207.70..
1.178.d:
भरतोऽपि महातेजाः स समेत्य युधाजिता ॥
अभ्यधावत तत्प्रीत्या मातुलं कैकयाधिपम् ॥1.207.70॥

1.178.m:
Having arranged the encampments of the lords of men and assigned all pleasures to them, / that moon of the lineage of Raghu, overjoyed, entered his maternal uncle's city on an elephant.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then Bharata, devoted to dharma, with a small retinue, / ran forward, and then, out of love, his maternal uncle, the lord of the Kekayas,
taking Bharata by the neck and smelling his head repeatedly, / also taking Bharata, came to the house, O king.
Overjoyed, he entered the city of his maternal uncle Yudhājit, / crowded with banners and flags, sprinkled with sandalwood water,
suffused all around with the incense of the essence of agallochum, / with offerings of five-coloured flowers made everywhere,
filled with all kinds of merchandise, its young people adorned, / with mansions scraping the sky, resembling masses of white clouds,
with oblations and worship arranged in the temples of the deities, / resounding on all sides with the sound of loud musical instruments,

1.178.m:
its market streets crowded with all the townsfolk wishing to see [him], / with masses of people gathered closely on the royal road, O great king,
all residences empty, their occupants drawn away to the royal road, / and the mansions along the royal road occupied by crowds of women.
The glorious Bharata entered the city, mounted on the front of an elephant. / And upon the entrance of that Bharata, whose form was like that of the god of love,
women abandoned their household chores and went to the windows: / some with their limbs only half-anointed, some with collyrium applied to only one eye,
some with their hair tied up on one side, some with it only half-arranged, / some having taken wooden clogs on one foot,
the women rushed hastily, with leather sandals on the second; / likewise, others pushed aside those who had previously occupied the windows.
While others were proceeding, some swift women / quickly went from window to window, casting off their leather sandals.
The women made those windows fair-faced with their own faces, / their hands resembling lotus buds with fine conch bracelets half-inserted.

द्वितीयपाणिसंदर्शसमाक्रान्तैर्ययुः करैः ॥

ययुरेवापरास्तत्र पाणिसंश्लिष्टनीवयः ॥
कुसुमप्रकरं काश्चिदूहमानाः शिरोगतैः ॥ 16 ॥

सितासितेन रामाणां रमणीयेन राघवः ॥ 17 ॥
ययौ दृष्टिनिपातेन रज्यमान इवांशुमान् ॥
स चकर्ष तदा तासां पतितैर्नेत्ररश्मिभिः ॥18 ॥
हृदयान्निगृहीत्वेव गच्छमानः स राघवः ॥
स तु दृग्विषये यासां यासां तस्मात्परागतः॥19॥
न ता बुबुधिरे काञ्चित्क्रियां चित्रगता इव ॥
भरते दूरयातेऽपि निश्चेष्टाः काश्चिदेव ताः ॥ 1.208.20 ॥
आकृष्टास्ता ययुः क्षोणीं प्रेर्यमाणैः सखीजनैः ॥
प्रद्युम्नांशसमुत्पन्नः प्रद्युम्नसमदर्शनः ॥ 21 ॥
आदाय तासां चेतांसि ययौ गजगृहं द्रुतम् ॥
तस्मिन्राजगृहे राजन्राघवो राजमन्दिरम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.178.m:
They went with hands occupied in viewing their other hand, / their minds confused by the loosening of the knot of their skirts.
Others went there holding their skirts with their hands; / some, carrying a shower of flowers on their heads,
hurried to the windows with their long garments trailing. / By the charming dark-and-white [glances] of the beautiful women, the descendant of Raghu
passed by, as though being coloured by the falling of their glances, like the sun. / Then, with the rays of their eyes that fell upon him,
that descendant of Raghu, as he went, seemed to seize and draw away their hearts. / But whenever he passed beyond the range of their sight,
they were unaware of any action, as if depicted in a painting. / Even when Bharata had gone far away, some remained motionless;
pulled by their companions, they went down to the ground. / Born from a portion of Pradyumna, appearing like Pradyumna,
having taken their hearts, he swiftly went to the elephant stable. / In that Rājagṛha, O king, the descendant of Raghu reached the royal palace,

आससाद महातेजाः कैलासमिव चापरम् ॥
प्रविश्य स गृहं मुख्यं प्रेषयामास भूभुजम् ॥ 23 ॥

उवास स सुखं तत्र पूजितश्च युधाजिता ॥

जाम्बूनदे रत्नसहस्रचित्रे स राजपुत्रः शयने विचित्रे ॥
सुष्वाप रात्रौ भवने विचित्रे निदाघरात्रिं पवने विचित्रे ॥ 25 ॥

1.178.m:
of great splendour, resembling a second Kailāsa. / Entering the principal palace, he sent for the king
and drinks, food, and clothing for the soldiers, O descendant of Yadu. / He dwelt there happily, honoured by Yudhājit; / and the sun, having the lustre of a cluster of hibiscus flowers, set.
On a wondrous bed of gold adorned with thousands of jewels, / in a wondrous palace, the prince slept at night, in the wondrous breeze of a summer night.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / At the end of that night, in the camps of the kings, / signal drums were sounded separately, O descendant of Yadu,
with various signs in their respective divisions for many leaders of the army. / Their clamorous sound rose into the sky.
Then the awakeners entered Bharata's presence: / lute players, principal singers, those skilled in playing flute instruments,
players of the mṛdaṅga, players of the paṇava, and blowers of conches, / melodious ones with impassioned voices, and reciters of auspicious verses,

1.178.d:
सूतमागधमुख्याश्च बन्दिनश्च नराधिप ॥
तुष्टुवुर्भरतं वीरं सुखसुप्तं महामतिम् ॥ 5 ॥
सुप्रभातं समुत्तिष्ठ प्रभाता रजनी शुभा ॥
दिक्प्राची रघुशार्दूल वर्ततेऽरुणरञ्जिता ॥ 6 ॥
नूनमस्यां हि वेलायां मातलिस्त्रिदशाधिपम् ॥
विबोधयति राजेन्द्र सुखाय जगतां विभुम् ॥ 7 ॥
त्वयि सुप्ते जगत्सुप्तं विबुद्धे च सुखान्वितम् ॥
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ लोकानां शिवाय रघुनन्दन ॥ 8 ॥
त्वं हि सर्वगुणारामो यथा रामो महीपतिः ॥
गुणैः शशाङ्करश्म्याभैस्त्वया वै रञ्जितं जगत् ॥9॥
अत्याश्चर्यं महाबाहो यशसा सुसितेन ते ॥
मुखान्यरातिवृन्दानां क्रियन्ते मलिनानि यत् ॥1.209.10॥
कृपाणधारापानीयं दृष्ट्वाऽरातिगणस्तव ॥
तृष्णयैव भवत्याशु रञ्जितानिलयो भयात् ॥ 11 ॥
अक्षोभ्यश्चातिगम्भीरो भवान्रत्नाकरस्तथा ॥॥।
अग्राह्यत्वात्समुद्रेण न समः प्रतिभाति नः ॥12॥
1.178.m:
and leading sūtas, māgadhas, and bards, O lord of men. / They praised the heroic, highly intelligent Bharata who was sleeping happily:
"Good morning! Arise! The auspicious night has dawned. / The eastern quarter, O tiger among the Raghus, is coloured red by the dawn.
Surely at this hour Mātali awakens the lord of the gods, / the lord of the worlds, for the happiness [of all], O king of kings.
When you are asleep, the world is asleep; and when you are awake, it is endowed with happiness. / Therefore arise, O delighter of the Raghus, for the welfare of the worlds!
For you are the delight of all virtues, just like King Rāma; / the world has indeed been delighted by you with virtues resembling the rays of the moon."
It is a great wonder, O strong-armed one, that through your exceedingly white fame / the faces of the hosts of your enemies are made dark.
Seeing the water that is the edge of your sword, your enemy host, / out of fear, quickly has its home reddened merely by thirst.
You are unshakeable, exceedingly deep, and likewise a mine of jewels; / yet since you cannot be grasped, you do not seem to us equal to the ocean.

1.178.d:
सौम्यः कलावाम्̐ल्लक्ष्मीवान्नयनानन्दकारकः ॥
(दोषाकरेण क्षयिणा नौपम्यं ते नराधिप) ॥13॥
बाहुभोज्यातिविस्तीर्णा सर्वाश्रयवती दृढा ॥
नौपम्यं याति ते सम्यक् क्षोणी विन्ध्येन कम्पिना ॥ 14 ॥
यत्तेऽस्ति तदवश्यं त्वं ददासि रिपुसूदन॥
अविद्यमाना भीर्दत्ता भवतारिगणे कुतः ॥15 ॥
निमेषमपि यो दृष्टस्त्वयापाङ्गनिरीक्षणैः ॥
समग्रदृष्ट्या य दृष्टो नित्यमेवेक्षणैः श्रियः ॥। 16 ॥
क्षुरपर्यन्तधारेण चक्रेणारिगणस्य ते ॥
शिरांस्यपहरत्याजौ देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥ 17 ॥
कपालमाली खट्वाङ्गी शशाङ्ककृतभूषणः ॥।
वामार्धदयिताकारः शङ्करः शं करोतु ते ॥18॥
पद्मासनः पद्मजन्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः ॥
ऋद्धिं मेधां धृतिं लक्ष्मीं बलं च विदधातु ते ॥ 19॥
नभश्चरोऽम्बुजो देवो दिग्वधूकरपूरकः ॥
ब्रह्माण्डमण्डपे दीपः सुप्रभातं करोतु ते ॥ 1.209.20 ॥
1.178.m:
Gentle, endowed with the arts, fortunate, delighting the eyes— / there is no comparison for you, O king of men, with the moon, which is a source of blemishes and wanes.
Vast, to be enjoyed by your arm, furnishing refuge to all, and firm, / your earth bears no proper comparison to the shaking Vindhya.
Whatever you possess, you certainly give away, O slayer of foes; / whence then was non-existent fear bestowed by you upon the host of enemies?
He who is looked upon by you with sidelong glances for even a moment, / is looked upon constantly by the glances of Fortune with her full gaze.
With his discus whose edge is sharp as a razor, Janārdana, the god of gods, / carries away in battle the heads of your enemy host.
Wearing a garland of skulls, bearing a skull-topped staff, adorned with the moon, / his left half having the form of his beloved—may Śaṅkara bring you welfare!
Seated on a lotus, born from a lotus, the grandfather of all the worlds— / may he grant you prosperity, intelligence, resolve, fortune, and strength!
Moving through the sky, born of water, a god filling the hands of the maidens that are the directions, / a lamp in the pavilion of the universe—may he bring you an auspicious dawn!

1.178.d:
केशयक्षेशदेवेशप्रेतेश्वरनिशाचराः ॥
सर्वदेवगणैः सार्धं सुप्रभातं दिशन्तु ते ॥ 21 ॥
ऋषयः सरितः शैलाः सागराश्च दिशो दश ॥
कालस्यावयवाश्चैव सुप्रभातं दिशन्तु ते ॥ 22 ॥
इति शृण्वन्गिरं पुण्यामेषां मङ्गलवादिनाम् ॥
महापुण्याहघोषेण तत्याज शयनं तदा ॥23॥
आयव्ययं स शुश्राव लेखकैर्गणकैः सह ॥
वेगोत्सर्गं ततः कृत्वा ययौ स्नानगृहं शुभम् ॥ 24 ॥
स्नानारम्भं ततश्चक्रे दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ॥
उत्सादितः कषायेण बलवद्भिर्नरैस्तदा ॥ 25 ॥
सुखं भद्रासनासीनः सूक्ष्माम्बरधरः प्रभुः ॥
सस्नौ स विविधैस्तोयैर्नदीसागरजैः शुभैः ॥ 26 ॥
कुम्भैः सुवर्णमाहेयैस्ताम्रै रौप्यमयैस्तथा ॥
शताधिकैर्महाराज सर्वौषधि समन्वितैः ॥ 27 ॥
क्षीरप्रवाहसंयुक्तैर्माल्यकण्ठैः सुपूजितैः ॥
आवर्जितैर्महीपाल सुस्नातालङ्कृतैर्नरैः ॥ 28 ॥
1.178.m:
May Śiva, the lord of Yakṣas, the lord of gods, the lord of the dead, and the night-roaming spirits, / along with all the hosts of gods, grant you an auspicious dawn!
May the sages, rivers, mountains, oceans, the ten directions, / and the divisions of time grant you an auspicious dawn!
Hearing this holy speech of these chanters of benedictions, / accompanied by the loud chant of an auspicious day, he then arose from his bed.
He listened to the income and expenditure together with the scribes and accountants; / then, having discharged the bodily urges, he went to the auspicious bath-chamber.
Then, having first cleansed his teeth, he began his bath; / he was then rubbed down with an astringent paste by strong men.
Seated comfortably on an auspicious seat, wearing a fine garment, the lord / bathed with various pure waters born of rivers and oceans,
With more than a hundred jars, O great king, made of gold, clay, / copper, and silver, accompanied by all kinds of medicinal herbs,
Endowed with streams of milk, their necks adorned with garlands, highly honored, / poured out, O protector of the earth, by well-bathed and adorned men,

1.178.d:
चन्दनस्रावसम्पूर्णैर्द्विजमन्त्रानुमन्त्रितैः ॥
बभार वसनं चारु स्नानतोयौघसङ्कुलम् ॥ 29 ॥
शशाङ्कमण्डलं पूर्णं तन्वभ्रैरिव संवृतम् ॥
वाद्यपुण्याहघोषेण तथा गीतस्वनेन च ॥ 1.209.30 ॥
स्नात्वोपस्पृश्य विधिवत्पूर्वां सन्ध्यां समाहितः ॥
ददर्श वदनं चारु दर्पणे चाथ सर्पिषि ॥ 31 ॥
स सुवर्णे महाराज दैवज्ञेनाभिमन्त्रिते ॥
दिनेशं तिथिनक्षत्रं ततः शुश्राव राघवः ॥ 32 ॥
सांवत्सरमुखोद्गीर्णं कलिदुःस्वप्ननाशनम् ॥
चकाराभ्यर्चनं चाथ देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥ 33 ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपूदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥
स्तवैर्बलिप्रदानैश्च गीतवाद्यस्वनेन च ॥ 34 ॥
संपूज्य देवदेवेशं विवेशाग्निगृहं शुभम् ॥
तत्राग्निं समुपस्थाय हुतं पूर्वं पुरोधसा ॥ 35 ॥
1.178.m:
Filled with sandalwood extract, consecrated with the mantras of twice-born [priests]. / He wore a beautiful garment drenched with the abundance of bath-water,
Like the full disc of the moon veiled by thin clouds, / to the sound of musical instruments and the chant of an auspicious day, and likewise to the sound of songs.
Having bathed, having sipped water according to rule, collected in mind at the morning twilight, / he then looked at his handsome face in a mirror and in clarified butter,
And in gold, O great king, consecrated by the astrologer. / Then the descendant of Raghu listened to the [ruling] deity of the day, the lunar day, and the lunar mansion,
Uttered from the mouth of the astrologer, which destroys the bad dreams of the Kali age. / Then he performed the worship of the discus-bearing god of gods,
With an abundance of perfumes, garlands, obeisance, incense, lamps, and food, / with hymns of praise, offerings, and the sound of songs and musical instruments.
Having worshipped the god, the lord of gods, he entered the auspicious fire-chamber; / there he approached the fire previously offered into by the family priest.

1.178.s:
duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ karma siddhivṛddhijayapradam ..

modakaiśca tathā ratnairvastraiśca raghunandanaḥ ..
pūjitānāṃ dvijendrāṇāṃ bharatena mahātmanā .. 41 ..

sa pūjayitvā viprendrānpraviśya ca tathā gṛham .. 42 ..
1.178.d:
दुःस्वप्ननाशनं कर्म सिद्धिवृद्धिजयप्रदम् ॥
प्रागेव तस्य कृतवान्विद्वान्नृपपुरोहितः ॥ 36 ॥
(ततस्त्वौपसमे वह्नौ भरतः प्रीतमानसः ॥)
श्रीसूक्तं पौरुषं सूक्तं जुहाव प्रयतस्तदा ॥ 37 ॥
आज्येन मन्त्रपूतेन विधिना सुसमाहितः ॥
दत्त्वा पूर्णाहुतिं चाग्नौ कृतजप्यो महामतिः ॥ 38 ॥
उदकेनार्चनं चक्रे देवानां पितृभिः सह ॥
ततः स निर्ययौ तस्माद्भरतो वह्निवेश्मनः ॥ 39 ॥
निष्क्रम्य पूजयामास ब्राह्मणान्वसुना तदा ॥
गोभिरश्वैः सुवर्णेन दधिपुष्पफलान्वितैः॥1.209.40॥
मोदकैश्च तथा रत्नैर्वस्त्रैश्च रघुनन्दनः ॥
पूजितानां द्विजेन्द्राणां भरतेन महात्मना ॥ 41 ॥
पुण्याहघोषस्त्रिदिवं जगाम मधुरस्वरः ॥
स पूजयित्वा विप्रेन्द्रान्प्रविश्य च तथा गृहम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.178.m:
The wise royal priest had already performed for him beforehand / the rite that destroys bad dreams and bestows accomplishment, prosperity, and victory.
Then, with a pleased mind, in the domestic fire, Bharata, / restrained, then made oblations reciting the Śrīsūkta and the Pauruṣasūkta,
With clarified butter purified by mantras according to rule, fully concentrated; / having offered the final oblation into the fire, the highly intelligent one, having performed his silent recitation,
Performed the worship of the gods together with the ancestors using water. / Then Bharata went out from that fire-chamber.
Having stepped out, he then honored the brahmins with wealth, / with cows, horses, and gold, accompanied by curds, flowers, and fruits,
And with sweetmeats, jewels, and garments, the descendant of Raghu [honored them]. / For the foremost of the twice-born honored by the great-souled Bharata,
The sweet-voiced chant of an auspicious day went up to heaven. / Having honored the foremost of the brahmins and entered the house,

1.178.d:
नित्यकर्म च कृत्वेदं चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ॥
सूक्ष्मशुक्लपरीधानो वरधूपेन धूपितः॥ 43 ॥
आभूष्य सर्वगात्राणां भूषणानि रघूद्वहः ॥
शुक्लं सुगन्धि माल्यं च स्रजश्च विविधास्तथा ॥ 44 ॥
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा निश्चक्राम सभागृहम् ॥
क्लृप्तं शय्यासनं तत्र वररत्नविभूषितम् ॥ 45 ॥
महार्घतोरणोपेतं सोत्तरच्छदमृद्धिमत् ॥
वितानञ्च तथा दत्तं तस्योपरि महर्द्धिमत् ॥ 46 ॥
आसीनमासने तस्न्निभरतं सत्यसंगरम् ॥
प्रांशवो बद्धनिस्त्रिंशाः कवचोत्तमभूषिताः ॥ 47 ॥
रक्ताम्बरधरा वीरा ररक्षुः पृष्ठसंस्थिताः ॥
तथैवोभयपार्श्वस्थाः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः ॥ 48 ॥
वारमुख्याः सुवेशास्तमुपासांचक्रिरे तदा ॥
बालव्यजनधारिण्यस्तालवृन्तकराः पराः ॥ 49॥
1.178.m:
And having performed this daily duty, [anointed] with fragrant sandalwood, / wearing a fine white garment, fumigated with excellent incense,
Having put on ornaments on all his limbs, the descendant of Raghu, / [wearing] a white, fragrant garland and various wreaths,
Having touched auspicious objects, went forth to the assembly-hall. / Prepared there was a couch and seat adorned with excellent jewels,
Furnished with a priceless archway, splendid with a counterpane; / and an exceedingly splendid canopy was placed above it.
As Bharata, true to his promise, was seated on that throne, / tall heroes bearing drawn swords, adorned with excellent armor,
And wearing red garments, guarded him, standing behind him; / likewise standing on both sides, with faces resembling the full moon,
Courtesans, beautifully dressed, attended upon him then, / some holding chowries, others with palm-leaf fans in their hands,

śreṇīmahattarā ye ca balamukhyāstathaiva ca ..
praveśayainānityukto dvāsthānkṣattā tato'bravīta .. 52 ..
brāhmaṇānbalamukhyāṃśca praveśayata satvaram ..
āśīrbhirabhinandyainaṃ saṃpraviṣṭā dvijottamāḥ .. 53 ..

tatastu balamukhyānāṃ namatāṃ bharataṃ tadā .. 54 ..

tatasteṣūpaviṣṭeṣu dvāreṣu vivṛteṣu ca .. 55 ..
praviveśa janaḥ sarvo na nyavāryeta kaścana ..
etasminneva kāle tu śuśruve tumulo dhvaniḥ .. 56 ...
1.178.d:
ताम्बूलभाण्डधारिण्यो नीलनीरजलोचनाः ॥
कुण्डली बद्धनिस्त्रिंशो दण्डपाणिः सुवेशवान् ॥ 1.209.50 ॥
उवाच भरतं क्षत्ता भूमिविन्यस्तजानुकः॥
दिदृक्षवस्ते संप्राप्ता ब्राह्मणाः संशयच्छिदः ॥ 51 ॥
श्रेणीमहत्तरा ये च बलमुख्यास्तथैव च ॥
प्रवेशयैनानित्युक्तो द्वास्थान्क्षत्ता ततोऽब्रवीत ॥ 52 ॥
ब्राह्मणान्बलमुख्यांश्च प्रवेशयत सत्वरम् ॥
आशीर्भिरभिनन्द्यैनं संप्रविष्टा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 53 ॥
बृसीषु दन्तपीठेषु विविशुश्च यथासुखम् ॥
ततस्तु बलमुख्यानां नमतां भरतं तदा ॥ 54 ॥
क्षत्ता जग्राह नामानि कण्ठारक्तस्वरान्वितः ॥
ततस्तेषूपविष्टेषु द्वारेषु विवृतेषु च ॥ 55 ॥
प्रविवेश जनः सर्वो न न्यवार्येत कश्चन ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु शुश्रुवे तुमुलो ध्वनिः ॥ 56 ॥।
1.178.m:
Holding betel vessels, with eyes like blue lotuses. / Wearing earrings, with a sword strapped on, holding a staff in hand, well-attired,
The chamberlain, placing his knees on the ground, said to Bharata: / "Brahmins who resolve doubts have arrived, wishing to see you,
As well as the elders of the guilds and the commanders of the army." / Told "Admit them," the chamberlain then said to the door-keepers:
“Admit the brahmins and army commanders quickly!” / Having greeted him with blessings, the foremost of the twice-born entered,
And sat down comfortably on mats of kuśa grass and ivory stools. / Then, as the army commanders bowed down to Bharata,
The chamberlain, with a voice sounding from his throat, announced their names.
Then, when they were seated and the doors were opened,
all the people entered; no one was turned away.
At that very moment, however, a tumultuous roar was heard,

1.178.s:
bharataṃ draṣṭukāmānāṃ bhūmipānāṃ mahātmanām ..
hrādena gajaghaṇṭānāṃ bṛṃhitena tathaiva ca .. 57 ..
hreṣitena turaṅgāṇāṃ rathanemisvanena ca ..
nāmabhiḥ kīrtyamānaiśca bandibhiḥ pṛthivīkṣitām .. 58 ..
śaṅkhavāditraghoṣeṇa paṭahānāṃ svanena ca ..
( ājagmurbharataṃ draṣṭuṃ narendrāḥ priyadarśanāḥ .. 59 ..
toraṇādavatīryaiva vāhanebhyo mahīkṣitaḥ) ..
sarve svalpaparīvārā viviśuste sabhāṃ śubhām .. 1.209.60 ..
śiraḥkampena bharataṃ namaskṛtya niveditāḥ ..
pratīhāreṇa dakṣeṇa tena cakurvarāsanam .. 61 ..
siṃhāsanasthānnṛpatīnbharatastvanurūpayan ..
girā papraccha kuśalaṃ pūjayāmāsa cāpyatha .. 62 ..
tuṣṭuvurvandinastatra nānādeśyānnarādhipān ..
nivedayantaḥ stutyante bharatāya mahātmane ..63..
stuvatāṃ bharataṃ tatra bandināṃ sa mahāsvanaḥ ..
prāsādabhogasaṃruddho vipulaḥ samapadyata .. 64 ..
1.178.d:
भरतं द्रष्टुकामानां भूमिपानां महात्मनाम् ॥
ह्रादेन गजघण्टानां बृंहितेन तथैव च ॥ 57 ॥
ह्रेषितेन तुरङ्गाणां रथनेमिस्वनेन च ॥
नामभिः कीर्त्यमानैश्च बन्दिभिः पृथिवीक्षिताम् ॥ 58 ॥
शङ्खवादित्रघोषेण पटहानां स्वनेन च ॥
( आजग्मुर्भरतं द्रष्टुं नरेन्द्राः प्रियदर्शनाः ॥ 59 ॥
तोरणादवतीर्यैव वाहनेभ्यो महीक्षितः) ॥
सर्वे स्वल्पपरीवारा विविशुस्ते सभां शुभाम् ॥ 1.209.60 ॥
शिरःकम्पेन भरतं नमस्कृत्य निवेदिताः ॥
प्रतीहारेण दक्षेण तेन चकुर्वरासनम् ॥ 61 ॥
सिंहासनस्थान्नृपतीन्भरतस्त्वनुरूपयन् ॥
गिरा पप्रच्छ कुशलं पूजयामास चाप्यथ ॥ 62 ॥
तुष्टुवुर्वन्दिनस्तत्र नानादेश्यान्नराधिपान् ॥
निवेदयन्तः स्तुत्यन्ते भरताय महात्मने ॥63॥
स्तुवतां भरतं तत्र बन्दिनां स महास्वनः ॥
प्रासादभोगसंरुद्धो विपुलः समपद्यत ॥ 64 ॥
1.178.m:
from the high-souled kings wishing to see Bharata,
by the ringing of elephant bells and likewise by their trumpeting,
by the neighing of horses, by the clatter of chariot rims,
and by the names of the rulers of the earth being proclaimed by bards,
by the blare of conches and musical instruments, and by the sound of drums.
The kings of pleasing appearance arrived to see Bharata.
Having dismounted from their mounts at the gateway itself,
the kings, all accompanied by small retinues, entered the splendid hall.
Having bowed to Bharata with an inclination of the head, and introduced
by the skilled doorkeeper, they took their excellent seats.
Accommodating the kings who were seated on their thrones,
Bharata inquired after their welfare in gentle words and then honored them.
Bards praised the rulers of men who had come from various regions there,
presenting them at the end of their praise to the high-souled Bharata.
That great sound of the bards praising Bharata there,
confined within the expanse of the palace, became immense.

1.178.s:
kṣmāpālamaulimāṇikyamarīcivikaṭojjvalam ..
bālātapāṃśucchuritaṃ babhūva ca sabhāgṛham .. 65 ..
tataḥ sa bharataḥ śrīmānvisasarja narādhipān ..
svahastadattatāmbūlānpratīhāraniveditān .. .. 66 ..
tataḥ samutthāya yayau dvitīyagṛhamuttamam ..
tatra cakre tadā mantraṃ mātulena yudhājitā .. 67 ..
purodhasā ca gārgyeṇa svena kālavidā tathā ..
yudhājiduvāca ..
kāle tvamīpsite prāpto gandharvāṇāṃ vadhecchayā .. 68 ..
tatra yāvanna jānanti gandharvāste tvadāgamam ..
avaskandena tānadya tāvadrātrau jahi prabho .. 69 ..
avaskandena nidhanaṃ sukhaṃ teṣāṃ bhaviṣyati ..
kālaviduvāca ..
supte pramatte viśvaste tathā rājañcchramā nvite .. 1.209.70 ..
avatīrṇe bale caiva saritaṃ vahatīṃ tathā ..
rātrau jāgaraṇaśrānte chadmayuddhaṃ vidhīyate .. 71 ..
1.178.d:
क्ष्मापालमौलिमाणिक्यमरीचिविकटोज्ज्वलम् ॥
बालातपांशुच्छुरितं बभूव च सभागृहम् ॥ 65 ॥
ततः स भरतः श्रीमान्विससर्ज नराधिपान् ॥
स्वहस्तदत्तताम्बूलान्प्रतीहारनिवेदितान् ॥ ॥ 66 ॥
ततः समुत्थाय ययौ द्वितीयगृहमुत्तमम् ॥
तत्र चक्रे तदा मन्त्रं मातुलेन युधाजिता ॥ 67 ॥
पुरोधसा च गार्ग्येण स्वेन कालविदा तथा ॥
युधाजिदुवाच ॥
काले त्वमीप्सिते प्राप्तो गन्धर्वाणां वधेच्छया ॥ 68 ॥
तत्र यावन्न जानन्ति गन्धर्वास्ते त्वदागमम् ॥
अवस्कन्देन तानद्य तावद्रात्रौ जहि प्रभो ॥ 69 ॥
अवस्कन्देन निधनं सुखं तेषां भविष्यति ॥
कालविदुवाच ॥
सुप्ते प्रमत्ते विश्वस्ते तथा राजञ्च्छ्रमा न्विते ॥ 1.209.70 ॥
अवतीर्णे बले चैव सरितं वहतीं तथा ॥
रात्रौ जागरणश्रान्ते छद्मयुद्धं विधीयते ॥ 71 ॥
1.178.m:
And the assembly hall became intensely radiant with the beams from the rubies in the diadems of the protectors of the earth,
as if sprinkled with the rays of the morning sun.
Then the glorious Bharata dismissed the rulers of men,
presented by the doorkeeper, after giving them betel with his own hand.
Then, rising up, he went to a second, supreme chamber.
There he held counsel with his maternal uncle Yudhājit,
and with his priest Gārgya, as well as with his astrologer.
Yudhājit said:
"You have arrived at the desired time, wishing to slay the Gandharvas.
Therefore, as long as those Gandharvas do not know of your arrival,
slay them tonight by a surprise attack, O Lord.
Their destruction will easily take place by means of a surprise attack."
The astrologer said:
"Against one asleep, careless, trusting, and likewise, O King, exhausted,
or when the army has disembarked and is crossing a flowing river,
or is worn out by staying awake at night—covert warfare is prescribed.

1.178.s:
rātrau vihāraśīlāste gandharvāḥ satataṃ prabho ..
na te'vaskandamarhanti rātrau kaikeyinandana .. 72 ..
vijayaśca divā yuddhe bharatasya pradṛśyate ..
gārgya uvāca ..
ādau dūtena vaktavyaṃ gandharvāṇāṃ prayojanam .. 73 ..
yathā deśamimaṃ tyaktvā vrajadhvaṃ tuhinācalam ..
gandharvāṇāṃ nivāsastu himavatyacalottame .. 74 ..
1.178.d:
रात्रौ विहारशीलास्ते गन्धर्वाः सततं प्रभो ॥
न तेऽवस्कन्दमर्हन्ति रात्रौ कैकेयिनन्दन ॥ 72 ॥
विजयश्च दिवा युद्धे भरतस्य प्रदृश्यते ॥
गार्ग्य उवाच ॥
आदौ दूतेन वक्तव्यं गन्धर्वाणां प्रयोजनम् ॥ 73 ॥
यथा देशमिमं त्यक्त्वा व्रजध्वं तुहिनाचलम् ॥
गन्धर्वाणां निवासस्तु हिमवत्यचलोत्तमे ॥ 74 ॥
1.178.m:
Those Gandharvas constantly roam about at night, O Lord;
they do not merit a surprise attack by night, O son of Kaikeyī.
Moreover, Bharata's victory is clearly foreseen in daytime battle."
Gārgya said:
"First, the purpose should be stated to the Gandharvas by an envoy:
'Leaving this region, go to the snowy mountain.
The dwelling of the Gandharvas on the Himavat, the best of mountains,

1.178.s:
pūrvameva kṛtastena yenedaṃ nirmitaṃ jagat ..
sthānametanmanuṣyāṇāṃ tyaktumarhatha mā ciram .. 75 ..
1.178.d:
पूर्वमेव कृतस्तेन येनेदं निर्मितं जगत् ॥
स्थानमेतन्मनुष्याणां त्यक्तुमर्हथ मा चिरम् ॥ 75 ॥
1.178.m:
was established long ago by Him by whom this universe was fashioned.
You ought to abandon this abode of humans without delay.'

1.178.s:
te ca dūtavacaḥ śrutvā sthānaṃ dadyurnarādhipa ..
asaṃśayamupāruhya caitanmama mataṃ bhavet .. 76 ..
1.178.d:
ते च दूतवचः श्रुत्वा स्थानं दद्युर्नराधिप ॥
असंशयमुपारुह्य चैतन्मम मतं भवेत् ॥ 76 ॥
1.178.m:
And upon hearing the envoy's word, they may yield the place, O ruler of men.
Without entertaining doubt, this should be my opinion."

1.178.s:
bharata uvāca ..
rāghavāḥ satyasandhāstu kūṭayuddhaṃ na śikṣitāḥ ..
tasmātteṣāṃ vadhaḥ kāryaḥ suyuddhena mayā nṛpa .. 77 ..
1.178.d:
भरत उवाच ॥
राघवाः सत्यसन्धास्तु कूटयुद्धं न शिक्षिताः ॥
तस्मात्तेषां वधः कार्यः सुयुद्धेन मया नृप ॥ 77 ॥
1.178.m:
Bharata said:
"The descendants of Raghu are true to their word and not trained in deceitful warfare.
Therefore, their slaying must be accomplished by me through fair battle, O King.

1.178.s:
gārgyavākyaṃ tathā buddhyā rocate'tiśayena me..
prayātu teṣāṃ dautyena gārgya eva mahāyaśāḥ .. 78 ..
1.178.d:
गार्ग्यवाक्यं तथा बुद्ध्या रोचतेऽतिशयेन मे॥
प्रयातु तेषां दौत्येन गार्ग्य एव महायशाः ॥ 78 ॥
1.178.m:
Likewise, Gārgya's counsel appeals to me exceedingly by its wisdom.
Let Gārgya himself, of great renown, proceed on an embassy to them."

1.178.s:
yudhājiduvāca ..
gaccha gārgya mahābhāga gandharvādhipatiṃ prati ..
taṃ ca śrāvaya vākyāni tvayoktānīha yāni me .. 79 ..
1.178.d:
युधाजिदुवाच ॥
गच्छ गार्ग्य महाभाग गन्धर्वाधिपतिं प्रति ॥
तं च श्रावय वाक्यानि त्वयोक्तानीह यानि मे ॥ 79 ॥
1.178.m:
Yudhājit said:
"Go, O highly fortunate Gārgya, to the lord of the Gandharvas,
and make him hear the words that you have spoken here to me.

1.178.s:
akriyāyāṃ tathā teṣāṃ śrāvayā'gryāṇi mā ciram ..
asyaiva nāmnā dharmajña bharatasya mahātmanaḥ .. 1.209.80 ..
1.178.d:
अक्रियायां तथा तेषां श्रावयाऽग्र्याणि मा चिरम् ॥
अस्यैव नाम्ना धर्मज्ञ भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥ 1.209.80 ॥
1.178.m:
And in the event of their non-compliance, recite foremost [threats] without delay,
in the very name of this high-souled Bharata, O knower of dharma."

1.178.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamastvityathokto'sau yayau gārgyo mahāyaśāḥ ..
rathena kāñcanāṅgena gandharvanagaraṃ prati .. 81 ..
1.178.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमस्त्वित्यथोक्तोऽसौ ययौ गार्ग्यो महायशाः ॥
रथेन काञ्चनाङ्गेन गन्धर्वनगरं प्रति ॥ 81 ॥
1.178.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having been told, 'So be it,' that highly renowned Gārgya
departed in a golden-bodied chariot toward the city of the Gandharvas.

1.178.s:
gate purohite gārgye bharato'pi mahāśayāḥ ..
hastipṛṣṭhe rathe cāśve śastre śāstre tathaiva ca .. 82 ..
1.178.d:
गते पुरोहिते गार्ग्ये भरतोऽपि महाशयाः ॥
हस्तिपृष्ठे रथे चाश्वे शस्त्रे शास्त्रे तथैव च ॥ 82 ॥
1.178.m:
When the priest Gārgya had departed, the noble-minded Bharata
engaged in exercise on an elephant's back, in a chariot, on a horse, with weapons and scriptures,

1.178.s:
vyāyāmaṃ ca tathā cakre niyuddhe ca yadūttama ..
utsāritastathā padabhyāṃ dhāvadbhiḥ kuśalairjanaiḥ ..83..
1.178.d:
व्यायामं च तथा चक्रे नियुद्धे च यदूत्तम ॥
उत्सारितस्तथा पदभ्यां धावद्भिः कुशलैर्जनैः ॥83॥
1.178.m:
and likewise in hand-to-hand combat, O best of the Yadus,
and was challenged on foot by skilled runners.

1.178.s:
snātaiḥ saṃpūjito viṣṇurvidhivatsāttvatottamaiḥ ..
namaskṛtya tathaivāgniṃ hutaṃ suṣṭhu purodhasā .. 84 ..
1.178.d:
स्नातैः संपूजितो विष्णुर्विधिवत्सात्त्वतोत्तमैः ॥
नमस्कृत्य तथैवाग्निं हुतं सुष्ठु पुरोधसा ॥ 84 ॥
1.178.m:
Having bathed, Viṣṇu was properly worshipped by the foremost Sātvatas;
and having bowed to the fire, an oblation was well poured by the priest.

1.178.s:
tathā bhuktavatāṃ śrutvā pūjitānāṃ dvijanmanām ..
puṇyāhaghoṣaṃ vittena bhūmipāla visarjya tān .. 85 ..
1.178.d:
तथा भुक्तवतां श्रुत्वा पूजितानां द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
पुण्याहघोषं वित्तेन भूमिपाल विसर्ज्य तान् ॥ 85 ॥
1.178.m:
Then, having heard the proclamation of an auspicious day by the twice-born who had dined and been honored,
and having dismissed them with wealth, O protector of the earth,

1.178.s:
parārdhyacandanāktāṅgastanucārusitāmbaraḥ ..
sarvālaṅkaraṇopetaḥ sragvī dhūpena dhūpitaḥ .. 86 ..
1.178.d:
परार्ध्यचन्दनाक्ताङ्गस्तनुचारुसिताम्बरः ॥
सर्वालङ्करणोपेतः स्रग्वी धूपेन धूपितः ॥ 86 ॥
1.178.m:
his body anointed with supreme sandalwood, clad in fine and beautiful white garments,
adorned with all ornaments, wearing garlands, and perfumed with incense,

1.178.s:
āsīnastvāsane divye bubhuje svajanairyutaḥ ..
mātulasya mahārghāṇi śucīni guṇavanti ca .. 87 ..
1.178.d:
आसीनस्त्वासने दिव्ये बुभुजे स्वजनैर्युतः ॥
मातुलस्य महार्घाणि शुचीनि गुणवन्ति च ॥ 87 ॥
1.178.m:
seated on a heavenly seat together with his kin, he partook
of his maternal uncle's costly, pure, and wholesome [food],

1.178.s:
aparīkṣitapūrvāṇi puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ ..
narapakṣimṛgāṇāntu liṅgairvahnau tathaiva ca .. 88 ..
1.178.d:
अपरीक्षितपूर्वाणि पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः ॥
नरपक्षिमृगाणान्तु लिङ्गैर्वह्नौ तथैव च ॥ 88 ॥
1.178.m:
previously tested by trustworthy men
by means of signs on humans, birds, and deer, and likewise in fire:

1.178.s:
bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca peyaṃ coṣyaṃ tathaiva ca ..
pātreṣu rukmaraupyeṣu tathā maṇimayeṣu ca .. 69 ..
1.178.d:
भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च लेह्यं च पेयं चोष्यं तथैव च ॥
पात्रेषु रुक्मरौप्येषु तथा मणिमयेषु च ॥ 69 ॥
1.178.m:
food to be chewed, food to be eaten, licked, drunk, and sucked,
served in vessels of gold, silver, and crystal.

1.178.s:
bhuktvānnaṃ gītaśabdena cāptaiḥ katipayaiḥ saha ..
tathopaspṛśya dharmātmā dantadhāvanapūrvakam .. 1.209.90 ..
1.178.d:
भुक्त्वान्नं गीतशब्देन चाप्तैः कतिपयैः सह ॥
तथोपस्पृश्य धर्मात्मा दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ॥ 1.209.90 ॥
1.178.m:
Having eaten the meal to the sound of song along with a few trusted companions,
and then having performed ablutions preceded by cleansing his teeth,

1.178.s:
cakrasya śayanaṃ bheje vāmapārśvena śatruhā ..
itihāsaṃ sa śuśrāva tatrasthaḥ puruṣottamaḥ .. 91 ..
1.178.d:
चक्रस्य शयनं भेजे वामपार्श्वेन शत्रुहा ॥
इतिहासं स शुश्राव तत्रस्थः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 91 ॥
1.178.m:
that slayer of foes, the righteous-minded Puruṣottama,
retired to the couch of the discus on his left side and listened to historical lore while lying there.

1.178.s:
tataḥ sa śayanaṃ tyaktvā śāstrābhyāsaṃ mahāyaśāḥ ..
cakāra raghuśārdūlaḥ satāṃ mārgamanuvrajan .. 92 ..
1.178.d:
ततः स शयनं त्यक्त्वा शास्त्राभ्यासं महायशाः ॥
चकार रघुशार्दूलः सतां मार्गमनुव्रजन् ॥ 92 ॥
1.178.m:
Then, rising from his bed, that tiger of the Raghus of great renown,
following the path of the virtuous, engaged in the study of the scriptures.

1.178.s:
etasminneva kāle tu saha gārgyo yudhājitā ..
viveśa bharataṃ draṣṭuṃ rathareṇupariplutaḥ .. 93 ..
1.178.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सह गार्ग्यो युधाजिता ॥
विवेश भरतं द्रष्टुं रथरेणुपरिप्लुतः ॥ 93 ॥
1.178.m:
At that very time Gārgya, covered with chariot dust,
entered along with Yudhājit to see Bharata.

1.178.s:
sukhāsīnaśca bharataṃ vākyametattato'bravīt ..
gārgya uvāca ..
tato vākyāni sarvāṇi śailūṣaḥ śrāvito mayā .. 94 ..
1.178.d:
सुखासीनश्च भरतं वाक्यमेतत्ततोऽब्रवीत् ॥
गार्ग्य उवाच ॥
ततो वाक्यानि सर्वाणि शैलूषः श्रावितो मया ॥ 94 ॥
1.178.m:
And sitting comfortably, he then addressed these words to Bharata.
Gārgya said:
"Thereupon all those words were made to be heard by Śailūṣa.

1.178.s:
na tāni tasya rocante saṃgrāmastasya rocate ..
bharatena samāgamya śvobhūte dvijapuṅgava .. 95 ..
1.178.d:
न तानि तस्य रोचन्ते संग्रामस्तस्य रोचते ॥
भरतेन समागम्य श्वोभूते द्विजपुङ्गव ॥ 95 ॥
1.178.m:
They do not please him; battle pleases him.
[He said:] 'Having encountered Bharata tomorrow, O bull among the twice-born,

1.178.s:
bharataṃ nāśayiṣyāmi nīhāraṃ candramā yathā ..
ityuktvā sa tu māṃ rājā preṣayāmāsa satvaraḥ .. 96 ..
1.178.d:
भरतं नाशयिष्यामि नीहारं चन्द्रमा यथा ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स तु मां राजा प्रेषयामास सत्वरः ॥ 96 ॥
1.178.m:
I shall destroy Bharata as the moon destroys the mist.'
Having spoken thus, that king sent me away in haste.

1.178.s:
āhvānadundubhistatra niṣkrānte mayi cāhataḥ ..
etajjñātvā sa yuddhāya prātaḥ sajjo bhavettava .. 97 ..
1.178.d:
आह्वानदुन्दुभिस्तत्र निष्क्रान्ते मयि चाहतः ॥
एतज्ज्ञात्वा स युद्धाय प्रातः सज्जो भवेत्तव ॥ 97 ॥
1.178.m:
And as I went forth, the drum of summons was beaten there.
Knowing this, let your army be ready for battle in the morning."

1.178.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
iti gārgyavacaḥ śrutvā bharato gārgyamabravīt..
gaccha śīghraṃ gṛhaṃ brahmañchrānto rathabalādhvataḥ ..98..
1.178.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इति गार्ग्यवचः श्रुत्वा भरतो गार्ग्यमब्रवीत्॥
गच्छ शीघ्रं गृहं ब्रह्मञ्छ्रान्तो रथबलाध्वतः ॥98॥
1.178.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having heard these words of Gārgya, Bharata said to Gārgya:
“Go home quickly, O brahmin; you are exhausted from the journey by chariot and army.

1.178.s:
ahamājñāpayiṣyāmi sarvaṃ sāṃgrāmikaṃ vidhim ..
etāvaduktvā vijayaṃ senādhyakṣamathā'bravīt..99..
1.178.d:
अहमाज्ञापयिष्यामि सर्वं सांग्रामिकं विधिम् ॥
एतावदुक्त्वा विजयं सेनाध्यक्षमथाऽब्रवीत्॥99॥
1.178.m:
I will order all the preparations for battle.”
Having said this much, he then addressed Vijaya, the commander of the army:

1.178.s:
mamoṣṭravāhibhiḥ śīghraṃ śibireṣu mahīkṣitām ..
yodhānājñāpayatvadya śvobhūtāya raṇāya vai .. 1.209.100 ..
1.178.d:
ममोष्ट्रवाहिभिः शीघ्रं शिबिरेषु महीक्षिताम् ॥
योधानाज्ञापयत्वद्य श्वोभूताय रणाय वै ॥ 1.209.100 ॥
1.178.m:
“Let my camel-riders quickly order the warriors
in the camps of the kings for battle tomorrow.

1.178.s:
yuddhāvadhānikaṃ sarvaṃ kartavyaṃ ca tathā tvayā ..
evamājñāpya nāgānāṃ turagāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 101 ..
1.178.d:
युद्धावधानिकं सर्वं कर्तव्यं च तथा त्वया ॥
एवमाज्ञाप्य नागानां तुरगाणां तथैव च ॥ 101 ॥
1.178.m:
And you must likewise attend to everything required for the fight.”
Having given this command, he inspected the elephants and horses,

1.178.s:
pratyāvekṣāṃ tataḥ kṛtvā sandhyāmanvāsya paścimām ..
rahogataḥ sa śuśrāva narāṇāṃ mūḍhabhāṣitam ..102 ..
1.178.d:
प्रत्यावेक्षां ततः कृत्वा सन्ध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम् ॥
रहोगतः स शुश्राव नराणां मूढभाषितम् ॥102 ॥
1.178.m:
and then, having performed the review and attended to the evening twilight devotion,
he retired to seclusion and heard the confused chatter of the men.

1.178.s:
āruroha tadā śrutvā prāsādaṃ himapāṇḍuram ..
kailāsaśikharākāraṃ nirvātaṃ rajanīmukhe .. .. 103 ..
1.178.d:
आरुरोह तदा श्रुत्वा प्रासादं हिमपाण्डुरम् ॥
कैलासशिखराकारं निर्वातं रजनीमुखे ॥ ॥ 103 ॥
1.178.m:
Hearing it, he then ascended at nightfall to a palace white as snow,
shaped like the peak of Mount Kailāsa and sheltered from the wind.

1.178.s:
tatastu sainikaḥ kaścicchibire bharatasya tu ..
talaṃ talenābhyahanatpavanārthaṃ yadṛcchayā .. 104 ..
1.178.d:
ततस्तु सैनिकः कश्चिच्छिबिरे भरतस्य तु ॥
तलं तलेनाभ्यहनत्पवनार्थं यदृच्छया ॥ 104 ॥
1.178.m:
Then a certain soldier in Bharata’s camp
struck palm against palm at will to create a breeze.

1.178.s:
tatastu sainikaiḥ sarvaistalatālairmahāsvanam ..
cakrire puruṣavyāghra tasminkāle divaṃ gatam .. 105 ..
1.178.d:
ततस्तु सैनिकैः सर्वैस्तलतालैर्महास्वनम् ॥
चक्रिरे पुरुषव्याघ्र तस्मिन्काले दिवं गतम् ॥ 105 ॥
1.178.m:
Thereupon, O tiger among men, all the soldiers with the clapping of their hands
made a great sound at that moment that reached up to the sky.

1.178.s:
pravavau ca tadānīto vāyurmanujapuṅgava ..
etasminneva kāle tu madrarājastadāṃśumān .. 106 ..
1.178.d:
प्रववौ च तदानीतो वायुर्मनुजपुङ्गव ॥
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मद्रराजस्तदांशुमान् ॥ 106 ॥
1.178.m:
And the wind, brought forth thereby, blew, O best of men.
At that very time, the radiant king of the Madras,

1.178.s:
prāsādavaramārūḍho jñātavānbharataṃ tadā ..
dīpālokena lakṣmyā ca prāsādasya vivṛddhayā .. 107 ...
1.178.d:
प्रासादवरमारूढो ज्ञातवान्भरतं तदा ॥
दीपालोकेन लक्ष्म्या च प्रासादस्य विवृद्धया ॥ 107 ॥।
1.178.m:
having climbed to the top of his excellent palace, noticed Bharata
by the light of lamps and the elevated splendour of the palace.

1.178.s:
sa jagāma tadā rājā prahasansainikaṃ janam ..
bharatasya pradāsyāmi yuktyaiva baladarśanam .. 108 ..
1.178.d:
स जगाम तदा राजा प्रहसन्सैनिकं जनम् ॥
भरतस्य प्रदास्यामि युक्त्यैव बलदर्शनम् ॥ 108 ॥
1.178.m:
Then that king went, laughing, to his soldiers:
“By a clever device I will show our strength to Bharata.

1.178.s:
tṛṇamuṣṭimupādīpya sarvo'pi kaṭake janaḥ ..
pāṇāvādāya muditaḥ kṣveḍāśabdaṃ karotu vai .. 109 ..
1.178.d:
तृणमुष्टिमुपादीप्य सर्वोऽपि कटके जनः ॥
पाणावादाय मुदितः क्ष्वेडाशब्दं करोतु वै ॥ 109 ॥
1.178.m:
Let every single person in the camp light a handful of grass,
take it in his hand, and joyfully raise a war-cry.”

1.178.s:
pārthivenaivamukte tu kaṭake tasya dhīmataḥ ..
solkāhasto janaḥ sarvaḥ kṣaṇena samapadyata .. .. 1.209.110 ..
1.178.d:
पार्थिवेनैवमुक्ते तु कटके तस्य धीमतः ॥
सोल्काहस्तो जनः सर्वः क्षणेन समपद्यत ॥ ॥ 1.209.110 ॥
1.178.m:
When the wise ruler had spoken thus in his camp,
all the men in an instant stood with torches in their hands.

1.178.s:
śibiraṃ madrarājñastu dvitīyamiva cāmbaram ..
babhūva tārakācitramulkāhastaistadā naraiḥ .. 111 ..
1.178.d:
शिबिरं मद्रराज्ञस्तु द्वितीयमिव चाम्बरम् ॥
बभूव तारकाचित्रमुल्काहस्तैस्तदा नरैः ॥ 111 ॥
1.178.m:
The camp of the king of the Madras then became like a second sky,
variegated with stars, by means of those men holding torches in their hands.

1.178.s:
tadbalaughamaparyantaṃ solkāhastairjanairvṛtam ..
dṛṣṭvā jagāma dharmātmā parāṃ prītiṃ raghūdvahaḥ .. 112 ..
1.178.d:
तद्बलौघमपर्यन्तं सोल्काहस्तैर्जनैर्वृतम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा जगाम धर्मात्मा परां प्रीतिं रघूद्वहः ॥ 112 ॥
1.178.m:
Seeing that boundless flood of an army surrounded by men holding torches,
the righteous-minded descendant of Raghu experienced supreme delight.

1.178.s:
kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāścaiva śrutvā harṣamupāgataḥ ..
tasminpraśānte jvalane mandībhūte ca nisvane .. 113 ..
1.178.d:
क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाश्चैव श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागतः ॥
तस्मिन्प्रशान्ते ज्वलने मन्दीभूते च निस्वने ॥ 113 ॥
1.178.m:
Hearing the war-cries and shouts of joy, he was filled with gladness.
When that blaze subsided and the noise diminished,

1.178.s:
abhyahanyanta bhūpānāṃ śibireṣu pṛthakpṛthak ..
saṃjñātūryāṇi ramyāṇi nānāliṅgāni cāpyatha .. 114 ..
1.178.d:
अभ्यहन्यन्त भूपानां शिबिरेषु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
संज्ञातूर्याणि रम्याणि नानालिङ्गानि चाप्यथ ॥ 114 ॥
1.178.m:
the charming signal-trumpets of various descriptions
were sounded individually in the camps of the kings.

1.178.s:
subahūni mahārāja tena kolāhalaṃ mahat ..
babhūva prītijananaṃ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ .. 115 ..
1.178.d:
सुबहूनि महाराज तेन कोलाहलं महत् ॥
बभूव प्रीतिजननं भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥ 115 ॥
1.178.m:
Very many they were, O great king, and from them arose a great clamour
that produced delight for the high-souled Bharata.

1.178.s:
mantrayitvā tataḥ śrīmānkṣaṇamātraṃ yudhājitā..
tenaiva saha bhuktvā ca suṣvāpa śayanottame ..
madhureṇa sugītena vīṇāveṇuraveṇa ca .. 116 ..
1.178.d:
मन्त्रयित्वा ततः श्रीमान्क्षणमात्रं युधाजिता॥
तेनैव सह भुक्त्वा च सुष्वाप शयनोत्तमे ॥
मधुरेण सुगीतेन वीणावेणुरवेण च ॥ 116 ॥
1.178.m:
Then the glorious one, having conferred for a mere moment with Yudhājit
and dined with him, went to sleep on an excellent bed
to the sweet sound of singing and the melody of lutes and flutes.

1.178.s:
himāvadāte varamālyacitre vitānakādhovihite manojñe ..
suṣvāpa rātriṃ sa mahānubhāvo bhogīndrabhoge madhujidyathaiva .. 117 ..
1.210
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
āhvānadundubhiṃ śrutvā śailūṣatanayāstataḥ ..
āseduḥ pārthivaṃ sarve śailūṣaṃ taṃ samāgatāḥ .. 1 ..
namuciḥ kāmapālaśca gaveṣaṇasudarśanau ..
vīrabāhuḥ subāhuśca vāyuvegasuvarcasau ..2..
nikumbhaḥ kumbhanāmā ca balāko balakastathā ..
harikeśo mahojāśca sūryaraśmiprabhaṅkaraḥ .. 3 ..
vṛndārako jyautiṣiko dṛḍhasyuraparājitaḥ ..
kumudaḥ kumudāpīḍo vasunāthaḥ sulocanaḥ .. 4 ..
candrāpīḍo gadī maulī kinnaro'jagaro ruhaḥ ..
kesarī varavāṇaśca bhānurāgāvaho rayiḥ ..5..
ekalavyo viśālaśca kalaviṅkaḥ kalāpriyaḥ ..
bhīmanādo mahānādo vāsukiḥ panaso gadaḥ .. 6 ..
1.178.d:
हिमावदाते वरमाल्यचित्रे वितानकाधोविहिते मनोज्ञे ॥
सुष्वाप रात्रिं स महानुभावो भोगीन्द्रभोगे मधुजिद्यथैव ॥ 117 ॥
1.210
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
आह्वानदुन्दुभिं श्रुत्वा शैलूषतनयास्ततः ॥
आसेदुः पार्थिवं सर्वे शैलूषं तं समागताः ॥ 1 ॥
नमुचिः कामपालश्च गवेषणसुदर्शनौ ॥
वीरबाहुः सुबाहुश्च वायुवेगसुवर्चसौ ॥2॥
निकुम्भः कुम्भनामा च बलाको बलकस्तथा ॥
हरिकेशो महोजाश्च सूर्यरश्मिप्रभङ्करः ॥ 3 ॥
वृन्दारको ज्यौतिषिको दृढस्युरपराजितः ॥
कुमुदः कुमुदापीडो वसुनाथः सुलोचनः ॥ 4 ॥
चन्द्रापीडो गदी मौली किन्नरोऽजगरो रुहः ॥
केसरी वरवाणश्च भानुरागावहो रयिः ॥5॥
एकलव्यो विशालश्च कलविङ्कः कलाप्रियः ॥
भीमनादो महानादो वासुकिः पनसो गदः ॥ 6 ॥
1.178.m:
Upon an attractive [bed], white as snow, adorned with choice garlands, prepared beneath a canopy,
that illustrious one slept through the night, just like the Slayer of Madhu on the coils of the lord of serpents.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Hearing the war-drum of challenge, all the sons of Śailūṣa
then assembled and approached the king, that Śailūṣa:
Namuci, Kāmapāla, Gaveṣaṇa, Sudarśana,
Vīrabāhu, Subāhu, Vāyuvega, Suvarcas,
Nikumbha, the one named Kumbha, Balāka, and Balaka,
Harikeśa, Mahaujas, Sūryaraśmiprabhaṅkara,
Vṛndāraka, Jyautiṣika, Dṛḍhasyu, Aparājita,
Kumuda, Kumudāpīḍa, Vasunātha, Sulocana,
Candrāpīḍa, Gadī, Maulī, Kinnara, Ajagara, Ruha,
Kesarī, Varavāṇa, Bhānurāgāvaha, Rayi,
Ekalavya, Viśāla, Kalaviṅka, Kalāpriya,
Bhīmanāda, Mahānāda, Vāsuki, Panasa, Gada,

1.178.s:
candravarmā mahāvarmā vasuṣeṇo'grajārakaḥ ..
ete cānye ca gandharvāḥ śailūṣasya sutāḥ prabhoḥ .. 7 ..
divyamālyāmbaradharā divyacandanabhūṣitāḥ ..
āsaneṣu mahārheṣu sabhāyāṃ viviśustadā .. 8 ..
śailūṣasya sutairguptā sabhā sā ratnacitritā ..
rarāja tārakā citrā niśeva nṛpa śāradī .. 9 ..
teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ śailūṣastānathābravīt ..
gārgyasya vacanaṃ sarvamanumānaṃ tathā svakam .. 1.210.10 ..
te'bhiyogaṃ tadā śrutvā mānuṣānmanujeśvara ..
cakrurnānāvidhāśceṣṭā manyunā krodhacetasaḥ .. 11 ..
gandharvarājaputrāste krodhādaśrupravarṣiṇaḥ ..
rejuryugāntameghābhā acirābhāsadṛgdṛśā .. 12 ..
babhāra namucirvaktraṃ krodharāgānurañjitam ..

1.178.d:
चन्द्रवर्मा महावर्मा वसुषेणोऽग्रजारकः ॥
एते चान्ये च गन्धर्वाः शैलूषस्य सुताः प्रभोः ॥ 7 ॥
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरा दिव्यचन्दनभूषिताः ॥
आसनेषु महार्हेषु सभायां विविशुस्तदा ॥ 8 ॥
शैलूषस्य सुतैर्गुप्ता सभा सा रत्नचित्रिता ॥
रराज तारका चित्रा निशेव नृप शारदी ॥ 9 ॥
तेषां समुपविष्टानां शैलूषस्तानथाब्रवीत् ॥
गार्ग्यस्य वचनं सर्वमनुमानं तथा स्वकम् ॥ 1.210.10 ॥
तेऽभियोगं तदा श्रुत्वा मानुषान्मनुजेश्वर ॥
चक्रुर्नानाविधाश्चेष्टा मन्युना क्रोधचेतसः ॥ 11 ॥
गन्धर्वराजपुत्रास्ते क्रोधादश्रुप्रवर्षिणः ॥
रेजुर्युगान्तमेघाभा अचिराभासदृग्दृशा ॥ 12 ॥
बभार नमुचिर्वक्त्रं क्रोधरागानुरञ्जितम् ॥
दिक्सौम्येव दिशादाहं महासंग्रामसूचकम् ॥ 13॥
कामपालललाटस्था त्रिशिखा भ्रुकुटी बभौ ॥
त्रिभिः प्रपातैर्गङ्गेव निपतन्ती हिमाचलम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.178.m:
Candravarmā, Mahāvarmā, Vasuṣeṇa, and Agrajāraka—
these and other Gandharvas were sons of the powerful Śailūṣa.
Wearing celestial garlands and garments, adorned with celestial sandalwood paste,
they then entered the assembly hall and sat upon costly seats.
Protected by Śailūṣa’s sons, that assembly hall, adorned with jewels,
shone, O king, like an autumn night variegated with stars.
When they were seated, Śailūṣa then told them
everything Gārgya had said, as well as his own assessment.
Hearing then of the assault from mortals, O lord of men,
their minds enraged, they made various gestures in fury.
Those sons of the Gandharva king, shedding tears of wrath,
resembled clouds at the end of an aeon, their eyes flashing like lightning.
Namuci wore a face flushed with the red of rage,
like the northern quarter during a forest fire foretelling a great battle.
The three-pointed knit of Kāmapāla’s brows on his forehead shone
like the Gaṅgā falling upon the Himalayas in three cascades.

1.178.d:
कृष्णे स शुक्लपर्यन्ते क्रोधरागानुरञ्जिते॥
कुमुदापीडनेत्रे तु सन्ध्या ताम्रे बभूवतुः ॥ 15 ॥
क्रोधाक्रान्तेन वपुषा कुमुदः कुमुदप्रभः ॥
रक्तोत्पलनिभाकारः क्षणेन समपद्यत ॥ 16 ॥
चन्द्रापीडमुखं चारु क्रोधधूम्रानुकारितम् ॥
बभार रूपं तन्वभ्रसंभृतस्य निशाभृतः ॥ 17 ॥
क्रोधनिश्वासधूमेन भानोर्वक्त्रमथावृतम् ॥
बभूव भानोः सदृशमुपरागे यदूत्तम ॥ 18 ॥
करनिष्पेषसंजातधूमधूम्रमुखाङ्गकः ॥
अन्वर्थनामतामाप तस्मिन्काले सुदर्शनः ॥ 19 ॥
गवेषणप्रवेगेन वह्निगर्भोज्ज्वलात्मना ॥
ताराभिवर्षणेनैव सूचितो भूपतिक्षयः ॥ 1.210.20 ॥
वीरबाहुभुजाघातरत्ननिष्पेषरेणुना ॥
विजृम्भितमथास्थाने क्रोधेनेव वपुष्मता ॥ 21 ॥
सुबाहुबाहुनिष्पेषो बभूवाशनिनिस्वनः ॥
निर्घात इव गम्भीरो राज्ञां निधनसूचकः ॥ 22 ॥
1.178.m:
Kumudāpīḍa’s eyes, black with white edges
and tinged with the red of rage, became coppery like twilight.
With his body overcome by anger, Kumuda, who had the splendour of a white lotus,
turned into the likeness of a red water-lily in an instant.
Candrāpīḍa’s handsome face, darkened with the smoke of anger,
assumed the appearance of the moon shrouded by thin clouds.
The face of Bhānu, veiled by the smoke of his angry breaths,
became like the sun during an eclipse, O best of the Yadus.
With his face and limbs darkened by the smoke born from wringing his hands,
Sudarśana, “Fair to Behold,” at that time gained an irony in his name.
By Gaveṣaṇa’s violent fury, blazing as if with fire within,
the destruction of kings was portended, just as by a shower of meteors.
By the dust of crushed jewels struck by the arms of Vīrabāhu,
an eruption occurred in the hall, as if wrath had assumed an embodied form.
The clash of Subāhu’s arms made a sound like a thunderbolt,
deep as an atmospheric crash portending the death of kings.

1.178.d:
वायुवेगमहावेगचरणोल्लिखिता क्षितिः ॥
विदद्रे पृथिवीपाल विनाशभयशंसिनी ॥ 23 ॥
आयासजातसंस्वेदपुलकोद्गमभूषितम् ॥
सुवर्चा धारयामास ललाटतटपट्टकम् ॥ 24 ॥
प्रस्विन्नगात्रसंक्रान्तकाञ्चनस्तम्भपिङ्गलः ॥
बभूव कुम्भनाभस्तु क्रोधो विग्रहवानिव ॥ 25 ॥
सुविनिःसृतरोमाग्निज्वालाकेसरमालिना ॥
नृसिंहवपुषश्चक्रे रविणानुकृतिर्हरेः ॥ 26 ॥
प्रस्वित्रगात्रसंक्रान्तसर्वगन्धर्वमण्डलः ॥
विश्वरूपधरं मौलः प्रजहास जनार्दनम् ॥ 27 ॥
गन्धर्वराजपुत्रास्ते मन्युना हृतचेतसः ॥
तदा बभूवुर्भूपाल सर्व एव विशेषतः ॥ 28 ॥
इत्थं सुतानां प्रसमीक्ष्य कोपं संस्मृत्य वाक्यानि पुरोहितस्य ॥
जगाम मन्युं सुतरां स राजा सन्दष्टदन्तच्छदभीमवक्त्रः ॥ 29 ॥
1.178.m:
The ground, scraped by the feet of Vāyuvega with great speed,
tore open, O protector of the earth, proclaiming the terror of destruction.
Suvarcas bore the expanse of his forehead,
adorned with the sprouting of bristling hair and perspiration born of exertion.
Tawny from the golden pillars reflected on his sweating limbs,
Kumbhanābha, indeed, was like wrath embodied.
Garlanded with manes of flames from the fire of his bristling hair that burst forth,
he imitated Hari of the form of Nṛsiṃha through his brilliance.
With the entire circle of Gandharvas reflected on his sweating body,
Maula laughed aloud at Janārdana bearing the universal form.
O king, all those sons of the Gandharva king
were then especially seized in their minds by fury.
Seeing thus the anger of his sons and recalling the words of the royal priest,
that king, whose terrible mouth bit his lip, gave way completely to fury.
